name: Ruscoe v Cryptopia Ltd (in liquidation)
forum: High Court of New Zealand (Christchurch Registry)
rule_or_holding: Crypto is property held on a separate express trust per coin. The theft loss is borne only by holders of the stolen coin types, pro rata, and the reference moment is THE DATE OF THE THEFT: liquidators determine the affected account holders and their shares 'as at the date of the theft'. Anyone who acquired the same coin AFTER the theft is carved out: no reduction for the theft is applied to them, and recoveries go only to those affected at the theft date.
relevance_to_gonka: The strongest court authority found for a snapshot at the incident: the class of people who bear/recover the hack loss is fixed at the moment of theft; later acquirers are outside the loss-sharing class (neither burdened nor entitled to recoveries). Supports treating pre-incident holders as the core protected class and later entrants as a separate category.
quote: [205](a) "as at the date of the theft, the liquidators should determine the accountholders affected and their relative shares in any trust of the digital assets which are the subject of the theft. The liquidators should then apply the loss from the theft pro rata to those existing holdings." [205](b) "to the extent that subsequent to the theft any accountholder acquired digital assets of the type that suffered the theft and those assets were added to the relevant trust assets, no reduction for the theft should be applied to that accountholder's share in the trust assets" [205](c) "any recoveries of cryptocurrency lost as a result of the theft should be applied pro rata to make up the loss suffered by such accountholders as were affected by it". Also [204]: "Those losses, as I see it, should be borne pari passu by those accountholders alone." Property/trust: [133], [187].

name: Ruscoe v Houchens (Re Cryptopia Ltd (in liq)) (Distribution) — hack losses and recoveries
citation: [2024] NZHC 419 (Palmer J, 1 March 2024); orders restated in the liquidators' 2026 draft orders, CIV-2023-485-411
forum: High Court of New Zealand (Wellington Registry)
rule_or_holding: Hack losses are topped up only up to 100% of the PRE-HACK holding and net of what the holder did afterwards: unclaimed holdings may be applied 'pari passu, to account for losses arising from the hack, up to 100 per cent of accepted pre-hack holdings, taking into account any post-hack transactions'; recoveries are distributed 'proportionate to the amount they lost in the hack and up to a maximum of 100% of the value of an account holder's holding in the stolen cryptocurrency as at the date of the hack, taking into account any later withdrawals'. The top-up reference balance is the balance 'as at 14 January 2019' (hack date).
relevance_to_gonka: Court-approved net-loss rule: compensation is capped at the pre-hack position and reduced by post-hack transactions, so nobody ends up better off than before the hack. Directly supports a 'nobody profits from the hack' cap and a hack-date reference balance.
quote: [40](c): "pari passu, to account for losses arising from the hack, up to 100 per cent of accepted pre-hack holdings, taking into account any post-hack transactions." Order 9.2(b): "proportionate to the amount they lost in the hack and up to a maximum of 100% of the value of an account holder's holding in the stolen cryptocurrency as at the date of the hack, taking into account any later withdrawals". [45]: "to reimburse account holders proportionately on the basis of the valuation as at the date of the hack."

name: Ruscoe v Houchens (Re Cryptopia) — entitlement date, soft cut-off and final cut-off
citation: [2024] NZHC 419, orders 1.1, 2.2-2.6 (as varied; Final Cut-off Date later moved to 30 September 2025)
rule_or_holding: Entitlement date = 14 May 2019 (start of liquidation), not the hack date. Two-stage deadline: a 'Soft Cut-off' (after at least 90 days' notice by email, website and social media) after which liquidators may proceed as if non-registered holders do not exist, but late claimants 'would still receive a distribution' from what remains; then a 'Final Cut-off' after which incomplete claims are treated as abandoned — yet the liquidators keep an express DISCRETION to accept late claims if it does not prejudice the administration.
relevance_to_gonka: A court-sanctioned gradient: full rights before the notified date, residual/discretionary treatment after it. Structurally the same as 'obligation before the warning, discretion after'. Note the cut-off was preceded by formal multi-channel notice of at least 90 days — a much more robust notice than a single X post.
quote: Order 1.1: "the Liquidators may adopt 14 May 2019 as the date at which the entitlement of each account holder of the respective cryptocurrency trusts shall be calculated." Order 2.5: "This order does not prevent the Liquidators, in the exercise of their discretion, from receiving, considering, resolving and / or accepting a claim after the passing of the Final Cut-off Date". Notice, para 10: "If you, as an account holder, register a claim after [Soft Cut-Off Date] you would still receive a distribution, but only if there is still cryptocurrency in the relevant trust(s) after trust administration costs have been removed."

name: WazirX (Zettai Pte Ltd) — reversal of post-halt trades and court-sanctioned scheme
citation: WazirX announcement of 8 August 2024; scheme of arrangement of Zettai Pte Ltd sanctioned by the Singapore High Court in October 2025 (judgment citation not verified)
forum: Exchange decision; later Singapore High Court (scheme of arrangement under the Companies Act 1967)
rule_or_holding: The exchange set the reference moment at its own official action — the withdrawal halt on 18 July 2024, 1 PM IST (07:30 UTC) — restored every portfolio to that moment and voided all trades made after it (18-21 July), including fees and referrals. Losses were then socialised through the scheme.
relevance_to_gonka: Closest precedent for using the project's official action/announcement time (not the hack transaction) as the cut-off, with every later trade treated as ineffective. Difference: a custodial exchange can technically reverse internal trades; on-chain DEX trades cannot be reversed, only left uncompensated.
quote: "All users will have their portfolio balances on the WazirX platform restored to what they were on July 18, 2024"; "All trades following July 18, 07:30 am UTC, are rendered ineffective"; aim: an "equitable outcome for users following the abnormality arising" from the hack (as quoted by Cointelegraph, 8 Aug 2024).

name: In re FTX Trading Ltd. — estimation of digital asset claims
citation: Case No. 22-11068 (JTD), Bankr. D. Del., Memorandum Opinion and Order of 26 June 2024 (Re: D.I. 5202); earlier bench ruling of 31 January 2024 approving petition-date pricing
forum: US Bankruptcy Court, District of Delaware (Judge John T. Dorsey)
rule_or_holding: Claims are valued at a single statutory reference moment — the petition date — 'as if the bankruptcy had never occurred' (11 U.S.C. § 502(b)); later price movements are ignored. Prices were derived from a weighted median over the 60 minutes before the petition time (per secondary reports).
relevance_to_gonka: Shows the standard legal technique: one fixed reference timestamp for valuing every claim, chosen by rule rather than by who would benefit. It is a valuation date, not an eligibility cut-off for post-incident traders.
quote: "As with any estimation, the value of the claims must be determined as of the petition date as if the bankruptcy had never occurred. 11 U.S.C. § 502(b)." (Opinion, p. 1)

name: In re Celsius Network LLC — petition-date dollarisation of account-holder claims
citation: Case No. 22-10964 (MG), Bankr. S.D.N.Y. (plan confirmed November 2023)
forum: US Bankruptcy Court, Southern District of New York (Chief Judge Martin Glenn)
rule_or_holding: Per secondary sources, claims were fixed in US dollars at petition-date prices via a conversion table; ballots were stated in dollars at petition-date prices. For the CEL token the petition-date market price ($0.81) was NOT used because the market was found to be dislocated/unreliable; a settlement value of about $0.25 was approved instead.
relevance_to_gonka: Second example of a fixed valuation date, plus a caution: a market price observed in a dislocated market at the reference moment may be replaced by a different value. Relevant if the WGNK price around the cut-off was manipulated or illiquid.
quote: No verbatim quote verified.

name: Re Quadriga Fintech Solutions Corp. (QuadrigaCX) — conversion date of cryptocurrency claims
citation: Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List), endorsement of Hainey J., 1 March 2021 (neutral citation not verified)
forum: Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List), bankruptcy of Quadriga
rule_or_holding: All cryptocurrency claims converted to Canadian dollars as of the date of bankruptcy (15 April 2019), by analogy with foreign-currency debts under BIA s. 215.1; one pooled date for about 17,000 claims for efficiency. The choice shifted value between fiat and crypto claimants (reported: fiat claims about 23% lower, crypto claims about 14% higher than under the February date).
relevance_to_gonka: A single uniform reference date is chosen on principle even though it visibly favours one group over another; courts accept that any date creates winners and losers.
quote: "His Honour ordered that claims made in cryptocurrency be converted as of the date of bankruptcy." (Stikeman Elliott note, 13 April 2021)

name: Mt. Gox — claim valuation dates in bankruptcy and civil rehabilitation
citation: Tokyo District Court, bankruptcy (commenced 24 April 2014) and civil rehabilitation (commenced June 2018) of MtGox Co., Ltd.; trustee Nobuaki Kobayashi
rule_or_holding: In bankruptcy, BTC claims were converted to yen at about ¥50,058.12 per BTC (price just before bankruptcy commenced, reported as CoinDesk BPI at 23:59 UTC on 23 April 2014). After the switch to civil rehabilitation in 2018, claims were re-valued at ¥749,318.83 per BTC (rate at commencement of rehabilitation). Creditors holding claims at the later proceeding benefited from the later date; claims were freely assignable, so claim buyers also benefited.
relevance_to_gonka: Reference date = commencement of the formal process, not the hack. Also a caution against assuming 'nobody profits': changing the reference date and allowing claim transfers produced large gains for late claim buyers.
quote: No verbatim quote verified.

name: Mt. Gox bitcoin ownership case
citation: Tokyo District Court, Civil Division 28, judgment of 5 August 2015, Heisei 26 (Wa) 33320
rule_or_holding: Bitcoin is not a tangible thing and cannot be the object of ownership under the Civil Code; the customer has only a bankruptcy claim, valued under insolvency rules. Nothing on post-incident participants.
relevance_to_gonka: Counter-example to the common-law 'crypto is property' line: in a civil-law setting victims may be mere creditors, which makes a negotiated/community compensation scheme more important than proprietary remedies.
quote: "the bitcoin does not have a physical existence, so that it does not constitute a "tangible thing," nor can be the object of ownership. Thus, the plaintiff does not have ownership of the Bitcoin, nor a right of segregation based on any such ownership." (English paraphrase/translation, Digital Assets Project, University of Oxford)

name: BitGrail (BG Services S.r.l.) bankruptcy
citation: Tribunale di Firenze, Sezione fallimentare, sentenza n. 18/2019, published 21 January 2019 (number/date as reported by Altalex; another source cites 17/2019)
rule_or_holding: The exchange and its owner were declared bankrupt; crypto treated as fungible goods held on an irregular deposit, so customers are creditors for equivalent units; the operator was held responsible for the shortfall. No cut-off or post-incident-trader ruling identified.
relevance_to_gonka: Context only: operator liability for a custody shortfall; no guidance on reference moment.
quote: No verbatim quote from the judgment verified. Press: the founder "must declare bankruptcy, forfeit personal assets, and return as much of the stolen digital assets as possible" (The Next Web, 28 Jan 2019, reporting documents shared by a victims' group).

name: Bitfinex hack — 36.067% socialised loss and BFX tokens
citation: Bitfinex announcements of 6-8 August 2016; BFX tokens fully redeemed 3 April 2017 (no court involvement)
rule_or_holding: Every account balance — including accounts holding no bitcoin — was reduced by 36.067% and credited with a transferable BFX token per dollar lost. The tokens traded at a deep discount (reported $0.49-0.65 for much of 2016) and were redeemed at $1 in April 2017, so whoever held the token at redemption was paid, regardless of whether they were an original victim.
relevance_to_gonka: Shows (i) loss socialisation at a single moment and (ii) the opposite of a net-loss rule: once the claim is a tradable bearer token, post-incident buyers of the claim profit. If Gonka wants 'nobody profits from the hack', claims must attach to addresses/positions at the cut-off, not to a transferable token.
quote: "Upon logging into the platform, customers will see that they have experienced a generalized loss percentage of 36.067%"; "This is the closest approximation to what would happen in a liquidation context." (Bitfinex, as quoted by Computerworld, 8 Aug 2016)

name: Coincheck NEM hack — compensation at a fixed reference price
citation: Coincheck announcement of 27/28 January 2018; refunds paid March 2018
forum: Exchange decision under supervision of Japan's FSA (no court)
rule_or_holding: Compensation in yen to all customers who held NEM on the platform at the time of the unauthorised transfer, at ¥88.549 per XEM — a volume-weighted average price on another exchange (Zaif) measured from Coincheck's trading halt (26 Jan 2018 12:09 JST) to the announcement (27 Jan 23:00 JST). Trading in NEM was halted, so there were no post-incident buyers on the platform.
relevance_to_gonka: Eligible class fixed at the moment of the theft; the price is not the pre-hack price but an average over the window between the platform's official action and its compensation announcement. Useful precedent for an averaged reference price instead of a single tick.
quote: No verbatim English quote verified. Japanese press quoting the release: 「算出期間は、CoincheckにおけるNEMの売買停止時から本リリース時までの加重平均の価格で、JPYにて返金いたします。」 (as surfaced in search results).

name: Youbit (Yapian) hack and bankruptcy filing
rule_or_holding: All customer balances were marked down to 75% as of the incident, with the remainder to follow after the bankruptcy settlement (insurance and sale of the business). Uniform haircut on balances at the incident moment; no post-incident trading class.
relevance_to_gonka: Context: socialised haircut at the incident moment.
quote: No verbatim quote verified.

name: Ankr aBNBc infinite-mint exploit — snapshot, 'do not trade' warning and exclusion of post-exploit speculation
citation: Ankr, 'The aBNBc Token Report' (2 December 2022) and after-action report (20 December 2022)
rule_or_holding: Ankr fixed one snapshot (2 Dec 2022 00:43:18 UTC, described as identifying holders 'before' the exploit), re-issued a new token (ankrBNB) to holders as of the snapshot and bought BNB to compensate affected liquidity providers. It explicitly told users not to trade or speculatively buy the token and stated that trading after the exploit would not be compensated: 'All trades done after this time will not affect the holder's reimbursement' (Cointelegraph paraphrase).
relevance_to_gonka: The closest factual analogue (unbacked mint, price collapse, continued trading, explicit warning). Ankr used a HARD cut-off — and placed it at the exploit snapshot, i.e. earlier than its own warning. Post-exploit buyers got nothing. Gonka's proposal (obligation up to the warning, discretion after) is more generous than Ankr's.
quote: "Do not trade aBNBc or speculatively buy it at a discount." "We understand diluted aBNBc was speculatively traded after the exploit occurred, but we are only able to compensate LP's caught off guard by the event." "Our snapshot taken on Dec-02-2022 12:43:18 AM +UTC will identify you if you are an affected LP." "We will use a snapshot and airdrop the newly-released ankrBNB tokens to all valid aBNBc holders before the snapshot."

name: pNetwork pGALA (BNB Chain) incident — two snapshots
citation: pNetwork, 'pGALA post-mortem: measures taken to safeguard the ecosystem from malicious actors and recovery plan' (November 2022); Gala v. pNetwork lawsuit (filed 2023)
jurisdiction: DeFi bridge (BNB Chain); US lawsuit by Gala
rule_or_holding: Two-tier plan as reported: (1) new pGALA re-issued 1:1 to holders as of the pre-drain snapshot; (2) a SECOND snapshot on 7 November 2022 08:00 UTC — four days after the incident and warning — for distributing the BNB recovered in the drain to holders of the now-uncollateralised pGALA (0.00000109 BNB per pGALA); any transfer after the second snapshot is void for the plan. So people who bought after the incident but before the announced second cut-off got a refund-type payment from the drained funds, not the full pre-incident value. The BNB leg was reported 'on hold' in 2023 and Gala sued pNetwork.
relevance_to_gonka: A real two-tier model: full restoration for pre-incident holders, a lesser pro-rata refund for post-incident buyers up to a later, publicly announced cut-off, nothing after it. Supports a gradient rather than a single hard line — and shows the post-incident tier was only the return of money actually recovered.
quote: As surfaced by search from the pNetwork post: "Any on-chain transfer of pGALA happening on BSC after the second snapshot will not be taken into account and thus will be considered void in the scope of the recovery plan." Press paraphrase of the warning: pNetwork told users to "consider the existing pancakeswap pool to be invalid" and not buy pGALA (Cryptopolitan).

name: Cover Protocol infinite-mint exploit — snapshot at the last pre-exploit block
citation: Cover Protocol compensation plan (announced 29-31 December 2020); snapshot at Ethereum block 11,541,218
rule_or_holding: Snapshot at 'the last transaction block before the exploit began'; new COVER issued 1:1 to holders and LPs as of that block; returned ETH distributed to pre-exploit LPs. Anyone who bought after the snapshot was outside the protocol's plan.
relevance_to_gonka: Classic snapshot-at-hack model: the protocol's own obligation runs only to pre-exploit holders.
quote: "the Cover Protocol team took a snapshot at block height 11,541,218, the last transaction block before the exploit began." "tokenholders will receive new COVER coins on a one-to-one ratio with their initial wallet balance before the hack." (Cointelegraph, 31 Dec 2020)

name: Binance SAFU compensation for users who bought COVER after the exploit snapshot
citation: Binance announcement of 31 December 2020 (SAFU Fund, US$10,107,505)
rule_or_holding: Binance, at its own discretion and from its own insurance fund, compensated users who bought COVER on Binance after the snapshot time and suffered losses, using the moment Binance HALTED TRADING as the outer limit ('We will also incorporate the time that COVER trading was halted on Binance'). Reported exclusion: no compensation for users who merely deposited tokens between the snapshot and the halt.
relevance_to_gonka: Precedent for exactly the proposed two-layer logic: the issuer's obligation stops at the exploit snapshot; trades between the exploit and the venue's official stop are covered by a separate, voluntary (discretionary) pool. Here the grace window ends at the official halt — the functional equivalent of the 'Do not trade WGNK' warning — and the payer was the venue, not the protocol.
quote: "Binance will utilize the Binance SAFU Fund to recompense a total of $10,107,505 USD" "(distributed in 8,171,634.10 BUSD and 2,581.16 ETH) to affected and eligible users"; "We will also incorporate the time that COVER trading was halted on Binance" (Binance, as quoted by Decrypt, 31 Dec 2020).

name: The DAO attack and Ethereum hard fork
citation: SEC, Report of Investigation Pursuant to Section 21(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934: The DAO, Release No. 81207 (25 July 2017)
forum: Ethereum community hard fork (20 July 2016); facts recorded by the US SEC
rule_or_holding: The hard fork moved all funds to a recovery contract where 'DAO Token holders could exchange their DAO Tokens for ETH'. There was no holder snapshot at the attack: redemption followed the token, so anyone holding DAO tokens at redemption — including people who bought at a discount after the attack was public — was made whole.
relevance_to_gonka: CONTRADICTS a cut-off model: in the best-known precedent, post-incident buyers were treated identically to original holders (and profited). The distinguishing feature is that the remedy restored the asset's backing in full; it did not compensate trading losses. It also means pre-attack holders who panic-sold after the attack got nothing.
quote: "The Hard Fork had the effect of transferring all of the funds raised (including those held by the Attacker) from The DAO to a recovery address, where DAO Token holders could exchange their DAO Tokens for ETH." "All DAO Token holders who adopted the Hard Fork could exchange their DAO Tokens for ETH, and avoid any loss of the ETH they had invested." (pp. 9-10)

name: Nomad bridge hack — pro-rata bridge-back of recovered funds
jurisdiction: DeFi bridge (Ethereum and others); no court
forum: Bridge operator recovery process (KYC via CoinList)
rule_or_holding: Whoever holds madAssets, passes KYC and bridges back receives a non-transferable NFT entitling them to a pro-rata share of recovered funds. No snapshot and no condition on when the madAssets were acquired was stated in the sources seen.
relevance_to_gonka: CONTRADICTS a cut-off by acquisition time: the claim follows the wrapped token, so post-hack buyers of discounted wrapped assets share equally with original holders. (It is a partial recovery, shared pro rata; nobody is made whole.)
quote: The protocol "will allow users to bridge back madAssets and access a pro-rata share of recovered funds" (Cointelegraph, 8 Dec 2022, citing Nomad's guide).

name: Euler Finance — redemption of returned funds
citation: Euler governance forum, 'Plan for Redemption of Euler Funds V2' (12 April 2023)
rule_or_holding: Each sub-account's position is frozen at 'the block the protocol was disabled' (immediately after the hack): liabilities are notionally repaid at that block, and the resulting net asset value is the claim. Claims are capped (NAV x 1.005 at redemption-time prices); the excess goes to a 'foregone profit' pool for those who would otherwise have gained, instead of being spread as a windfall.
relevance_to_gonka: Returned-funds case like Gonka's: the claim was defined by the position at the block of the protocol's own emergency action, and the plan contains an explicit anti-windfall cap. Positions could not be traded after the pause, so there was no post-incident trading class.
quote: "For each sub-account, Euler simulates the repayment of all liabilities at the block the protocol was disabled." NAV is computed using "a secure pricing method snapshot taken at a pre-announced future "redemption" block."

name: KyberSwap Elastic exploit — Treasury Grant Program
forum: Protocol treasury grant (explicitly a grant, with KYC)
rule_or_holding: Affected assets are valued in USD 'at the last block prior to the Primary Exploit' (or prior to the relevant follow-on drain). Only liquidity providers whose assets were taken or locked (Categories 1, 2 and 4) qualify; other categories are outside the grant. Users choose 60% over 3 months or 100% over 12 months, or opt out. Grant terms include a refund obligation if assets are later recovered. The programme is framed as a voluntary treasury grant, not as a debt. Swappers/post-exploit traders are not addressed.
relevance_to_gonka: Reference value at the last pre-exploit block; compensation labelled a grant (discretionary); built-in refund if funds are recovered — a net-loss/no-double-recovery device.
quote: Reference value "as quoted on CoinGecko at the last block prior to the Primary Exploit"; the Grant Terms "will include Treasury Grant refund requirements in the event that some or all Affected Assets are recovered."

name: Balancer v2 exploit — distribution of rescued funds
citation: Balancer governance, '[BIP-892] Distribution of Rescued Funds from Balancer v2 November 3rd 2025 Attacks' (posted 27 November 2025)
rule_or_holding: Eligibility is determined by pool-token (BPT) holdings at the 'last block before first exploit tx on each network' (e.g. Ethereum block 23717626). Distribution is non-socialised (each pool's rescued funds go only to that pool's LPs) and pro rata to holdings at the snapshot. 180-day claim window. Transfers of BPT after the exploit are not addressed — the pre-exploit snapshot makes them irrelevant.
relevance_to_gonka: Recent, primary-sourced example of the mainstream DeFi rule: the snapshot is the last block before the exploit; later holders are simply not in the class.
quote: Snapshot rule: "last block before first exploit tx on each network". "Pro-rata by BPT holdings — Distribution proportional to each holder's share of the pool's BPT at the snapshot block". "Non-socialized — Each affected pool's rescued funds are distributed only to LPs of that specific pool and network".

name: Beanstalk governance exploit — 'Unripe' assets for pre-exploit holders
rule_or_holding: Claims ('Unripe Beans', 'Unripe LP') were issued only to those who held 'in the block prior to the exploit', 1:1 to pre-exploit balances, vesting as the protocol was recapitalised.
relevance_to_gonka: Another primary-sourced snapshot at the last pre-exploit block.
quote: "Farmers who held Beans in the block prior to the exploit received 1 Unripe Bean for every pre-exploit Bean"

name: Eminence (EMN) exploit — distribution of funds returned by the hacker
citation: Yearn/Eminence refund, September-October 2020 (snapshot at Ethereum block 10954410)
rule_or_holding: The returned 8m DAI was distributed (about 50% refund) according to balances at 'a snapshot the block before the hack took place' (3,656 addresses). Later buyers were not in the snapshot.
relevance_to_gonka: Hacker-returned funds were allocated strictly by the last pre-hack block.
quote: "a forthcoming 50% refund as per balances taken at a snapshot the block before the hack took place" (Decrypt, 29 Sep 2020)

name: Terra 2.0 airdrop — pre-attack and post-attack snapshots with different weights
citation: Terra governance proposal 1623 and 'Terra 2.0 — LUNA Airdrop' (May 2022)
jurisdiction: Layer-1 blockchain; no court (not a hack — de-peg/collapse)
rule_or_holding: Two snapshots: 'Pre-attack' (block 7,544,910, 7 May 2022 14:59:37 UTC) and 'Post-attack' (block 7,790,000, 26 May 2022 16:38:08 UTC). New LUNA allocation: pre-attack LUNA holders 35%, pre-attack aUST holders 10%, post-attack LUNA holders 10%, post-attack UST holders 15%, community pool 30%. Post-incident buyers were included, but at a far lower per-token rate (reported Binance ratios: 1 LUNC pre-attack = 1.034735071 LUNA vs 1 LUNC post-attack = 0.000015307927 LUNA).
relevance_to_gonka: The best-known gradient: both groups recognised, pre-incident holders heavily favoured. Shows that a community may choose to give post-incident buyers something rather than nothing — supports 'discretionary', not 'excluded'. Not a hack and not a compensation of trading losses, so analogy is by structure only.
quote: No verbatim quote verified.

name: Elixir deUSD wind-down after the Stream Finance loss
rule_or_holding: Elixir took a snapshot of all remaining deUSD/sdeUSD balances at the time of its announcement; snapshotted balances are redeemable 1:1 for USDC through a claims portal; minting and redemptions were disabled. Purchases after the snapshot carry no claim. (Dip-buyers before the snapshot were paid $1.)
relevance_to_gonka: Precedent for a cut-off placed at the issuer's official announcement rather than at the triggering event. Caveat: it did not apply a net-loss test — whoever held at the snapshot was paid in full, including discount buyers.
quote: Elixir "has reportedly taken a snapshot of all remaining deUSD and sdeUSD holder balances", which "can be redeemed 1:1 for USDC when a claims portal opens" (The Block, 6 Nov 2025).

name: Hyperliquid JELLY incident — users made whole except flagged addresses
forum: Validator vote and Hyper Foundation reimbursement
rule_or_holding: All users were reimbursed by the Foundation automatically from on-chain data, EXCEPT addresses flagged as involved in the manipulation.
relevance_to_gonka: Precedent for excluding from compensation those who exploited the incident — supports carving out the attacker's counterparties, arbitrage bots and anyone who knowingly profited.
quote: "All users apart from flagged addresses will be made whole from the Hyper Foundation"; "This will be done automatically in the coming days based on onchain data." (as quoted by Cointelegraph, 26 Mar 2025)

name: Curve / Vyper re-entrancy exploit — DAO vote to reimburse LPs
citation: Curve DAO vote, December 2023 (about US$49.2m: US$7.2m recovered ETH + about US$42m vested CRV)
forum: DAO governance vote (about 94% in favour, as reported)
rule_or_holding: The DAO voted to make LPs of the affected pools whole for the shortfall remaining AFTER deducting recovered funds; the unrecovered part was paid in CRV vested for a year. Loss was computed per affected pool; secondary-market traders of the affected tokens were not part of the scheme.
relevance_to_gonka: Net-loss approach (compensation = loss minus recoveries) adopted by token-holder vote; compensation limited to those whose assets were in the exploited contracts.
quote: No verbatim quote verified.

name: Mango Markets exploit; United States v. Eisenberg
citation: Mango DAO vote of October 2022; United States v. Eisenberg, No. 23-cr-10 (S.D.N.Y.), Opinion and Order of 23 May 2025 (Subramanian J.)
forum: DAO governance settlement; US federal criminal court
rule_or_holding: The DAO used the returned funds plus treasury so that 'all mango depositors will be made whole' — compensation ran to depositors (by their balances at the exploit), not to MNGO secondary-market traders. The criminal ruling turned on venue and on the absence of a false representation to a permissionless protocol.
relevance_to_gonka: Returned-funds settlement by DAO vote; and a reminder that courts may not treat an on-chain exploit as fraud, so a community scheme should not depend on a legal finding of wrongdoing.
quote: Proposal wording as reported: "all mango depositors will be made whole".

name: Full-replenishment bridge cases: Wormhole (2022), Ronin (2022), Poly Network (2021)
citation: Wormhole: Jump Crypto replaced 120,000 ETH (February 2022). Ronin: Sky Mavis reimbursed 117,600 ETH and 25.5m USDC and reopened the bridge on 28 June 2022. Poly Network: attacker returned the funds (August 2021).
jurisdiction: DeFi bridges; no court (see separate entry for the Jump/Oasis court order)
rule_or_holding: No cut-off or snapshot was needed: once backing is restored token-for-token, every holder of the wrapped asset — whenever they acquired it — is whole. Ronin restored ETH and USDC in kind (dollar value at reopening was far below the hack-date value). None of these programmes compensated secondary-market trading losses of people who sold at depressed prices in the interim.
relevance_to_gonka: Sets the baseline: restoring the bridge reserves (as happened after the Gonka hacker's return) is what the industry treats as the bridge's core obligation. Compensation of interim trading losses goes beyond what Wormhole, Ronin or Poly did — which supports calling at least part of it discretionary.
quote: "Sky Mavis has now reimbursed 117,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC by providing the ETH liquidity to back users' Wrapped ETH (wETH) on the Ronin network" (as surfaced in search results).

name: Jump Crypto / Oasis counter-exploit of the Wormhole hacker under an English court order
citation: Order of the High Court of England and Wales received by Oasis on 21 February 2023 (order and any judgment not published; case name not verified)
forum: High Court of England and Wales
rule_or_holding: Not about cut-offs. Shows an English court ordering an intermediary with technical control to retrieve stolen crypto for the party who had already made victims whole (subrogation-like outcome).
relevance_to_gonka: Recovery by the party that funded compensation is recognised in practice: whoever pays victims can step into their shoes against the attacker and recovered assets.
quote: Oasis statement (as quoted by Blockworks): it "retain[s] no control or access to these assets."

name: Harmony Horizon bridge hack — reimbursement proposals
citation: Harmony reimbursement proposal (July 2022) and revised recovery plan (September 2022)
forum: Core team proposal to on-chain governance
rule_or_holding: The first plan would have minted 2.48-4.97bn ONE and paid it monthly 'based on the value of tokens lost when a snapshot of the blockchain is taken'; it was withdrawn after community backlash against inflation. The revised plan promised '0% minting' and treasury-funded recovery. Final outcome for holders not established.
relevance_to_gonka: Shows a community rejecting compensation that dilutes existing holders — relevant to how a Gonka compensation is funded — and that reimbursement was treated as a matter for governance, not as an automatic debt.
quote: Harmony stated the goal of "preserving the foundation of the Harmony blockchain with 0% minting" (as surfaced in search results).

name: Fantom Foundation Ltd v Multichain Foundation Ltd
forum: General Division of the High Court of Singapore (assessment of damages after default judgment)
rule_or_holding: Damages for the wrapped assets = their value on 6 July 2023 (the day before the breach) LESS their residual value on 18 September 2023. The court applied the general rule of valuing loss by reference to the date of breach, and expressly declined to use 8 July 2023 (the day after the incident became public) because prices that day were too volatile to be reliable. Award: US$58,620.55 on this head; US$2,187,870.55 in total.
relevance_to_gonka: A court judgment on a bridge collapse that (i) takes the last pre-incident day as the reference price, (ii) deducts the residual value of what the claimant still holds (net loss), and (iii) rejects post-incident panic prices as a measure. Strong support for a pre-hack reference price and a net-loss computation.
quote: [21] "the value of the wrapped assets on 6 July 2023, less any residual value on 18 September 2023." [22] the claimant "invites the court to assess the loss of value with reference to the date of the breach", "which is the general position on valuing compensatory damages for breach of contract in Singapore". [27] "I therefore accept that the damages claim should be valued at US$58,620.55."

name: PAID Network infinite-mint exploit
rule_or_holding: The team announced a new contract restoring all balances from a pre-hack snapshot; activity during the exploit was not covered, and the announcement reportedly did not say what would happen to people who bought during the dip.
relevance_to_gonka: Same pattern (pre-hack snapshot; post-exploit buyers unaddressed).
quote: No verbatim quote verified.

name: PancakeBunny flash-loan exploit — compensation of 'Original Holders'
rule_or_holding: Compensation (new pBUNNY token plus a fee-funded Compensation Pool) was promised to 'Original Holders' for the difference between the market cap at the time of the exploit and the retained value. Exact snapshot definition not verified.
relevance_to_gonka: Unbacked mint + price crash; compensation directed to pre-exploit holders only.
quote: As surfaced in search results: "We will compensate Original Holders for the difference between the market cap at the time of the exploit and the current retained value of $39M (the Losses) by issuing a new token, pBUNNY, and by creating a Compensation Pool."

name: AA v Persons Unknown, Re Bitcoin
rule_or_holding: Cryptoassets such as bitcoin are property and can be the subject of a proprietary injunction (held for the purposes of interim relief). Nothing on cut-offs.
relevance_to_gonka: Foundation for proprietary claims to stolen/extorted crypto in English law.
quote: [59] "I consider that a crypto asset such as Bitcoin are property." [61] "crypto currencies are a form of property capable of being the subject of a proprietary injunction."

name: Tulip Trading Ltd v van der Laan (Bitcoin Association for BSV and others)
citation: [2023] EWCA Civ 83 (Birss, Popplewell and Lewison LJJ, 3 February 2023)
rule_or_holding: Only that there is a serious issue to be tried on whether developers owe such duties; no finding that they do. The claim did not reach trial (reported discontinued in 2024 — not verified).
relevance_to_gonka: Those who control a protocol or bridge may arguably owe duties to asset holders after a hack; the point is unresolved, so it supports prudence, not a firm legal obligation.
quote: [91] "The conclusion is not that there is a fiduciary duty in law in the circumstances alleged by Tulip, only that the case advanced raises a serious issue to be tried."

name: Quoine Pte Ltd v B2C2 Ltd
citation: [2020] SGCA(I) 02 (Menon CJ, Phang JA, Prakash JA, French IJ, Mance IJ; 24 February 2020)
forum: Singapore Court of Appeal (appeal from the Singapore International Commercial Court)
rule_or_holding: By majority the trades stood: no operative mistake, no implied term allowing the platform to reverse trades executed at abnormal prices, and the reversal was a breach of the term that filled orders are irreversible. The court left open whether BTC can be held on trust.
relevance_to_gonka: CAUTION for any argument that trades at hack-distorted prices are legally void or must be unwound: absent an express term or actual knowledge of a mistake, trades at abnormal prices are binding and the counterparty may keep the gain. This points towards compensation funded by the community (ex gratia) rather than a legal clawback from those who traded during the dislocation.
quote: [7] "no operative mistake on the part of the Counterparties that could be relied upon to vitiate the Trading Contracts". [22] (platform terms) "once an order is filled, you are notified via the Platform and such an action is irreversible." [72] "the Proposed Implied Terms are inherently incompatible with the Irreversible Action Clause".

name: ByBit Fintech Ltd v Ho Kai Xin and others
forum: General Division of the High Court of Singapore
rule_or_holding: USDT is a thing in action capable of being held on trust; an institutional constructive trust arises over stolen assets at the time of the theft.
relevance_to_gonka: The victim's proprietary interest crystallises at the moment of theft — the legal analogue of a snapshot at the hack.
quote: [4] "Like any other thing in action, USDT is capable of being held on trust." [42] "An institutional constructive trust arises over stolen assets at time of the theft".

name: CLM v CLN and others
forum: General Division of the High Court of Singapore
rule_or_holding: Serious arguable case that stolen cryptoassets are property protectable by a proprietary injunction against persons unknown; disclosure orders against exchanges granted. Interlocutory.
relevance_to_gonka: Tracing and freezing of stolen crypto is available against unknown hackers and at exchanges.
quote: [46] the plaintiff proved "a serious arguable case that the Stolen Cryptocurrency Assets were capable of giving rise to proprietary rights" "which could be protected via a proprietary injunction".

name: Osbourne v Persons Unknown and Ozone Networks Inc
rule_or_holding: Realistically arguable that NFTs are property; injunction against persons unknown and a Bankers Trust disclosure order against the marketplace granted.
relevance_to_gonka: Further support for proprietary relief over stolen tokens and disclosure orders against platforms.
quote: [13] "there is at least a realistically arguable case that such tokens are to be treated as property as a matter of English law."

name: D'Aloia v Persons Unknown Category A and others (Bitkub)
citation: [2024] EWHC 2342 (Ch) (Richard Farnhill, Deputy High Court Judge, 12 September 2024)
forum: High Court, Chancery Division (first full trial of a crypto-fraud tracing claim)
rule_or_holding: USDT attracts property rights; but the claim failed because the claimant did not prove that his funds reached the exchange wallet. Tracing through a mixture is available only in equity; FIFO is not the only permissible method, but any method must be methodologically sound and properly evidenced. The judgment's issues summary treats the bona fide purchaser for value without notice defence as available in principle for USDT (though not made out by Bitkub on the facts).
relevance_to_gonka: Two lessons: (i) a compensation scheme based on on-chain tracing must use a documented, defensible methodology; (ii) the law's dividing line for innocent recipients is NOTICE — a purchaser without notice is protected, one with notice is not. An explicit official warning is the natural 'notice' moment, which is the legal logic behind treating post-warning traders differently.
quote: [5] "USDT attract property rights under English law." [6] "The Claimant has failed to show that any of his funds were received in the 82e6 wallet." [7(iii)] "other methods, if methodologically sound and properly evidenced, are available".

name: Cetus (Sui) exploit — validator vote and recovery plan
citation: Sui on-chain community vote closed 29 May 2025; Cetus recovery plan (June 2025)
forum: Validator governance vote; protocol recovery plan
rule_or_holding: Validators (about 90.9% in favour) moved the frozen funds to a multisig held in trust for affected accounts; with a US$30m Sui Foundation loan and treasury funds, LPs of the affected pools regained liquidity, and residual losses were covered by a compensation contract in vested CETUS (15% of supply). Compensation ran to LPs of exploited pools; no snapshot detail verified.
relevance_to_gonka: Context: compensation directed at those whose assets were in the exploited contracts; residual paid in vested native tokens.
quote: No verbatim quote verified.

name: Basic Inc. v. Levinson
rule_or_holding: Fraud-on-the-market: investors trading in an efficient market are presumed to rely on the integrity of the price. The presumption is rebutted if the truth credibly entered the market; those who trade after the corrective statements have no connection with the fraud.
relevance_to_gonka: Best single authority for the thesis: after a credible corrective statement, later traders fall outside the protected group. Qualifiers from the same passage: the correction must have 'credibly entered the market', and the Court declined to say how fast information is absorbed (fn. 28).
quote: if, despite petitioners' allegedly fraudulent attempt to manipulate market price, news of the merger discussions credibly entered the market and dissipated the effects of the misstatements, those who traded Basic shares after the corrective statements would have no direct or indirect connection with the fraud.

name: Halliburton Co. v. Erica P. John Fund, Inc. (Halliburton II)
rule_or_holding: Reaffirms Basic. To invoke the presumption the plaintiff must have traded between the misrepresentation and the time the truth was revealed; defendants may rebut by showing no price impact. Market efficiency is a matter of degree and of proof.
relevance_to_gonka: Element (4) is the class-period rule in one sentence: trade before 'the truth was revealed' or you are outside the class. The 'matter of degree' passage is the counter-point on speed of absorption.
quote: a plaintiff must prove that: (1) the alleged misrepresentations were publicly known, (2) they were material, (3) the stock traded in an efficient market, and (4) the plaintiff traded the stock between when the misrepresentations were made and when the truth was revealed.

name: Dura Pharmaceuticals, Inc. v. Broudo
rule_or_holding: An inflated purchase price is not itself a loss; the plaintiff must show an economic loss caused by the truth reaching the market (loss causation). Securities actions are not insurance against market losses.
relevance_to_gonka: Compensation should track realised economic loss attributable to the event, not every adverse price move; a compensation scheme is not market insurance, which supports declining to cover post-warning speculation.
quote: not to provide investors with broad insurance against market losses, but to protect them against those economic losses that misrepresentations actually cause.

name: PSLRA 90-day look-back limitation on damages
rule_or_holding: Market-price damages are capped at the difference between the price paid and the mean trading price during the 90 days beginning on the date the corrective information is disseminated (or until the plaintiff's earlier sale).
relevance_to_gonka: The dissemination date of the correction anchors the whole damages calculation, and Congress deliberately measured over a window after it because prices 'bounce back'. Relevant because the attacker returned almost everything: a mean-price look-back nets out the recovery. A statutory admission that markets need time after a disclosure.
quote: shall not exceed the difference between the purchase or sale price paid or received, as appropriate, by the plaintiff for the subject security and the mean trading price of that security during the 90-day period beginning on the date on which the information correcting the misstatement or omission that is the basis for the action is disseminated to the market.

name: Securities Act of 1933, § 11(a) and § 12(a)(2)
rule_or_holding: Liability for a false registration statement or prospectus runs to any acquirer except one who knew of the untruth at the time of acquisition.
relevance_to_gonka: Issuer-side liability is cut off, purchaser by purchaser, by knowledge at the time of acquisition. The standard is actual knowledge and under § 11 the defendant must prove it.
quote: any person acquiring such security (unless it is proved that at the time of such acquisition he knew of such untruth or omission) may, either at law or in equity, in any court of competent jurisdiction, sue

name: UK FSMA 2000, Schedule 10 paras 1(3), 3, 6 (and POATR 2024, Sch. 2 para 4)
citation: Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (c. 8), Sch. 10; S.I. 2024/105, Sch. 2
rule_or_holding: A person responsible for listing particulars or a prospectus is not liable for loss caused by a false statement if a correction was published before the securities were acquired, or if the claimant acquired with knowledge that the statement was false.
relevance_to_gonka: The most literal statutory statement of the thesis: published correction before acquisition means no liability to that acquirer. It also sets the quality bar for the correction and (para 1(3)(b)) recognises a period before it is 'reasonably practicable to bring a correction to the attention of persons likely to acquire'. In-force status of Sch. 10 versus the POATR successor was not checked; cite both.
quote: that before the securities in question were acquired, a correction had been published in a manner calculated to bring it to the attention of persons likely to acquire the securities

name: Germany, WpHG §§ 97, 98 (damages for late or untrue ad hoc disclosure)
forum: Statute (Bundestag); year is that of the current section numbering
rule_or_holding: The issuer compensates an investor who bought after the omission and still held when the information became known; no claim if the investor knew the information when trading.
relevance_to_gonka: Civil-law statute with the same architecture: the protected window closes when the information becomes known; knowledge at the time of the trade removes the claim (actual knowledge, 'kannte'). It also makes delay in publishing the issuer's responsibility, which supports treating the exploit-to-warning interval as an obligation.
quote: Der Anspruch nach Absatz 1 besteht nicht, wenn der Dritte die Insiderinformation im Falle des Absatzes 1 Nr. 1 bei dem Erwerb oder im Falle des Absatzes 1 Nr. 2 bei der Veräußerung kannte.

name: West Virginia Pipe Trades Health & Welfare Fund v. Medtronic, Inc.
forum: US District Court, District of Minnesota
rule_or_holding: A class period ends when a corrective disclosure or curative information is publicly announced or otherwise effectively disseminated to the market; the court shortened the class period to the first corrective disclosure.
relevance_to_gonka: Shows courts trimming the compensated group at the first effective disclosure; later repetitions of the same facts do not extend it. Opinion itself not opened.
quote: is publicly announced or otherwise effectively disseminated to the market

name: Ganino v. Citizens Utilities Co.
citation: 228 F.3d 154 (2d Cir. 2000), quoting In re Apple Computer Sec. Litig., 886 F.2d 1109, 1116 (9th Cir. 1989)
forum: US Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
rule_or_holding: The truth-on-the-market defence requires that corrective information be conveyed with enough intensity and credibility to counter-balance the misleading impression; the defence is intensely fact-specific.
relevance_to_gonka: Counter-point on notice quality: not any mention of the truth ends the protected period. The official, explicit 'Do not trade WGNK' scores well on credibility and explicitness; reach and timing (one channel, 00:24 UTC) are the weak points. Also explains why earlier third-party alerts are a weaker cut-off than the official post.
quote: the corrective information must be conveyed to the public "with a degree of intensity and credibility sufficient to counter-balance effectively any misleading information created by" the alleged misstatements.

name: SEC v. Texas Gulf Sulphur Co.
forum: US Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
rule_or_holding: News is not public the instant a release is read; insiders must wait until it could reasonably be expected to appear over the media of widest circulation, and the court noted the advisability of a reasonable waiting period for outsiders to absorb it.
relevance_to_gonka: Leading authority that publication and effective public knowledge are separated by a real interval. Argues against a to-the-second cut-off at the timestamp of the post and for a short grace window.
quote: at the minimum Coates should have waited until the news could reasonably have been expected to appear over the media of widest circulation, the Dow Jones broad tape

name: EU Prospectus Regulation, art. 23(2) (withdrawal right after a supplement)
citation: Regulation (EU) 2017/1129, art. 23(2), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2809
rule_or_holding: When a supplement correcting a prospectus is published, investors who had already agreed to buy may withdraw within two working days (three after the 2024 amendment) of publication.
relevance_to_gonka: Those protected are the ones who committed before the correction, and the legislator gives a fixed reaction window measured from publication. A model for a short, fixed grace period.
quote: shall have the right, exercisable within two working days after the publication of the supplement, to withdraw their acceptances

name: In re PolyMedica Corp. Securities Litigation
citation: No. 05-1220 (1st Cir. Dec. 13, 2005); reporter cite 432 F.3d 1 is from memory
forum: US Court of Appeals, First Circuit
rule_or_holding: For the fraud-on-the-market presumption an efficient market is one where the price fully reflects all publicly available information, meaning it responds so quickly that ordinary investors cannot profit from the news; this must be proved, using factors such as those in Cammer v. Bloom.
relevance_to_gonka: Counter-point: instant absorption is a property of proven-efficient markets. A thin, just-exploited DEX token would fail most efficiency factors, so the cut-off cannot rest on an assumption that the warning was absorbed at once.
quote: By "fully reflect," we mean that market price responds so quickly to new information that ordinary investors cannot make trading profits on the basis of such information.

name: Cammer v. Bloom (market-efficiency factors)
forum: US District Court, District of New Jersey
rule_or_holding: Five factors indicate an efficient market: weekly trading volume, analyst coverage, market makers and arbitrageurs, Form S-3 eligibility, and a cause-and-effect relationship between unexpected news and an immediate price response.
relevance_to_gonka: Checklist showing what courts require before presuming that news is impounded in price. Opinion not opened; factors taken from a NERA summary on the Harvard corporate governance forum.
quote: (5) a cause-and-effect relationship, over time, between unexpected corporate events or financial releases and an immediate response in stock price.

name: Patell & Wolfson, The intraday speed of adjustment of stock prices to earnings and dividend announcements
rule_or_holding: Initial price reaction within a few minutes; trading-rule profits dissipate within five to ten minutes; variance and serial-correlation disturbances persist for several hours into the next trading day.
relevance_to_gonka: Empirical time-scale for the best-covered market: minutes for the price, hours for the dust to settle. Supports a grace window of tens of minutes to a few hours, not days. Abstract opened; full paper not.
quote: The returns earned by simple trading rules dissipate within five to ten minutes, although significant returns are detected in the overnight period and at the opening of trading on the next day. Disturbances in the variance and serial correlation persist for several hours and extend into the following trading day.

name: Busse & Green, Market efficiency in real time
rule_or_holding: Prices respond to televised analyst reports within seconds; positive reports are incorporated within about one minute.
relevance_to_gonka: Shows how fast liquid markets can react to a broadcast signal. Figures come from a search summary only; neither the abstract nor the paper was opened.

name: British Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Co Ltd v Underground Electric Railways Co of London Ltd
rule_or_holding: The compensatory principle is qualified by the claimant's duty to take all reasonable steps to mitigate; damage due to neglect to do so is not recoverable.
relevance_to_gonka: Classic statement that avoidable loss after knowledge of the breach is the claimant's own. Quote taken from a scholarly article; the AC report was not reachable and secondary versions differ by a word or two.
quote: which imposes on a plaintiff the duty of taking all reasonable steps to mitigate the loss consequent upon the breach, and debars him from claiming any part of the damage which is due to his neglect to take such steps

name: Globalia Business Travel SAU v Fulton Shipping Inc of Panama (The New Flamenco), summarising The Elena D'Amico
rule_or_holding: Where there is an available market, loss or gain from the innocent party's decision to wait and speculate is not caused by the breach; it is for the innocent party's own account.
relevance_to_gonka: Sharper than mitigation for post-warning buyers: a new purchase after the warning is fresh speculation, not a failure to reduce an existing loss. The sentence is the Supreme Court's summary of Longmore LJ and Robert Goff J.
quote: If the innocent party chooses to speculate as to the way in which the market is going to go, the result of such speculation is for his account not the account of the guilty party.

name: Germany, BGB § 254 (contributory negligence and mitigation)
rule_or_holding: Where the injured person's fault contributed to the damage, or he failed to avert or mitigate it, liability and the extent of compensation depend on the circumstances, in particular on how far each side caused the damage.
relevance_to_gonka: Authority for a coefficient rather than a switch: civil law reduces compensation in proportion to each side's contribution. A declining percentage for post-warning trades is an apportionment in this sense.
quote: liability in damages as well as the extent of compensation to be provided depend on the circumstances, in particular on the extent to which the damage was caused mainly by one or the other party.

name: Russian Civil Code, art. 404 (creditor's fault) and art. 1083(2) (gross negligence of the victim)
forum: Statute (civil code); text read on an unofficial mirror
rule_or_holding: The court may reduce the debtor's liability if the creditor intentionally or negligently contributed to the increase of losses or did not take reasonable measures to reduce them; gross negligence of the victim reduces compensation in proportion to fault.
relevance_to_gonka: Same apportionment logic as BGB § 254: reduction, not automatic exclusion. Supports a coefficient for post-warning trades.
quote: Суд также вправе уменьшить размер ответственности должника, если кредитор умышленно или по неосторожности содействовал увеличению размера убытков, причиненных неисполнением или ненадлежащим исполнением, либо не принял разумных мер к их уменьшению.

name: CISG art. 77 (mitigation)
citation: UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods (1980), art. 77
rule_or_holding: A party relying on a breach must take reasonable measures to mitigate the loss; otherwise damages are reduced by the amount by which the loss should have been mitigated.
relevance_to_gonka: International consensus that loss avoidable after knowledge of the breach is not compensable. Presupposes knowledge, which is why the warning rather than the exploit is the trigger.
quote: If he fails to take such measures, the party in breach may claim a reduction in the damages in the amount by which the loss should have been mitigated.

name: UNIDROIT Principles of International Commercial Contracts 2016, art. 7.4.8
rule_or_holding: The non-performing party is not liable for harm that the aggrieved party could have reduced by taking reasonable steps; reasonable mitigation expenses are recoverable.
relevance_to_gonka: Same mitigation rule in transnational soft law; also supports reimbursing reasonable costs of people who acted on the warning.
quote: The non-performing party is not liable for harm suffered by the aggrieved party to the extent that the harm could have been reduced by the latter party's taking reasonable steps.

name: DCFR III.–3:705 (Reduction of loss)
citation: Draft Common Frame of Reference (2009), III.–3:705
forum: Study Group on a European Civil Code / Acquis Group
rule_or_holding: The debtor is not liable for loss the creditor could have reduced by taking reasonable steps.
relevance_to_gonka: European restatement of the mitigation rule; confirms it is common ground across civil and common law.
quote: The debtor is not liable for loss suffered by the creditor to the extent that the creditor could have reduced the loss by taking reasonable steps.

name: Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 350 (avoidability as a limitation on damages)
rule_or_holding: Damages are not recoverable for loss the injured party could have avoided without undue risk, burden or humiliation; reasonable but unsuccessful efforts to avoid loss do not bar recovery.
relevance_to_gonka: Avoidable loss is excluded, but subsection (2) protects someone who made reasonable efforts: a holder who sold after the warning to cut a pre-existing position was arguably mitigating, not speculating. Text read in a university course reproduction, not the ALI original.
quote: (1) Except as stated in Subsection (2), damages are not recoverable for loss that the injured party could have avoided without undue risk, burden or humiliation.

name: EU PSD2, arts. 69, 71, 73, 74 (unauthorised payment transactions)
rule_or_holding: The user must notify without undue delay; before notification the payer may bear up to EUR 50; after notification the payer bears no financial consequences (except fraud); gross negligence removes the cap; claims lapse after 13 months.
relevance_to_gonka: Notification is the statutory hinge that reallocates losses before and after it. Caveat: here the notice runs from user to provider, the reverse of Gonka; the analogy is of principle (loss shifts to the party that has been told and can act).
quote: The payer shall not bear any financial consequences resulting from use of the lost, stolen or misappropriated payment instrument after notification in accordance with point (b) of Article 69(1), except where the payer has acted fraudulently.

name: UK Payment Services Regulations 2017, regs 72, 74, 77
rule_or_holding: Payer liable up to £35 before notification; not liable for losses arising after notification; redress requires notification without undue delay and within 13 months.
relevance_to_gonka: Same before/after-notification allocation as PSD2 in UK law. Same direction caveat. As-made text read; later amendments not checked.
quote: the payer is not liable for any losses incurred in respect of an unauthorised payment transaction— (a) arising after notification under regulation 72(1)(b)

name: US Regulation E, liability of consumer for unauthorized transfers (tiered by time of notice)
forum: Federal regulation (CFPB; implements the Electronic Fund Transfer Act); year is that of the current codification
rule_or_holding: Notice within 2 business days of learning of the loss: liability capped at $50. Later: capped at $500. Failure to report a statement item within 60 days: unlimited liability for transfers after the 60 days that timely notice would have prevented. Time limits are extended for extenuating circumstances.
relevance_to_gonka: Clearest black-letter example of responsibility growing in steps with elapsed time after knowledge. Two features worth copying: the higher tiers reach only loss that would not have occurred with timely action, and there is an explicit extension for extenuating circumstances. Direction caveat as for PSD2.
quote: If the consumer notifies the financial institution within two business days after learning of the loss or theft of the access device, the consumer's liability shall not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers that occur before notice to the financial institution.

name: US Regulation Z, liability of cardholder for unauthorized use
forum: Federal regulation (implements the Truth in Lending Act); year is that of the current codification
rule_or_holding: Cardholder liability is capped at the lesser of $50 or the amount obtained by unauthorised use before notification to the card issuer.
relevance_to_gonka: A pure before/after-notification line with a nominal cap before it. Direction caveat as for PSD2.
quote: shall not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount of money, property, labor, or services obtained by the unauthorized use before notification to the card issuer

name: UCC Article 4A §§ 4A-202, 4A-203, 4A-204 (unauthorised payment orders)
rule_or_holding: An unauthorised order binds the customer if the bank followed a commercially reasonable security procedure in good faith; otherwise the bank refunds, but the customer loses interest if it does not notify within a reasonable time not exceeding 90 days. A notice counts only if received in time to act on it.
relevance_to_gonka: Another fixed time limit keyed to notification, plus a neat statement of the counter-principle: notice must arrive at a time and in a manner giving a reasonable opportunity to act.
quote: notice of which is not received at a time and in a manner affording the bank a reasonable opportunity to act on it before the payment order is accepted

name: UCC § 4-406 (customer's duty to discover and report unauthorised signature or alteration)
rule_or_holding: A customer who does not examine statements and report forgeries is precluded as to later forgeries by the same wrongdoer after a reasonable period not exceeding 30 days, and is absolutely barred after one year.
relevance_to_gonka: Step-function time limits (30 days, one year) running from the moment information was made available: loss shifts progressively to the party who had the information and did not act.
quote: after the customer had been afforded a reasonable period of time, not exceeding 30 days, in which to examine the item or statement of account and notify the bank

name: UCC § 8-210 (Overissue)
rule_or_holding: Securities issued beyond the issuer's power are not validated; the person entitled may compel the issuer to buy and deliver an identical genuine security or, if none is reasonably available, recover the price he or the last purchaser for value paid, with interest.
relevance_to_gonka: Nearest doctrinal twin of 22M unbacked WGNK: innocent holders get a genuine replacement or the price paid. Supports treating compensation of protected purchasers as an obligation and measuring it by price paid, not peak market value. Limits: WGNK is a bridge token and the over-mint was an attacker's act.
quote: If a security is not reasonably available for purchase, a person entitled to issue or validation may recover from the issuer the price the person or the last purchaser for value paid for it with interest from the date of the person's demand.

name: UCC §§ 8-202(b)(1), 8-205 (defective or unauthorised issue valid for a purchaser without notice)
rule_or_holding: A security issued with a defect going to its validity, or bearing an unauthorised signature, is valid or effective in the hands of a purchaser for value without notice of the defect.
relevance_to_gonka: The issuer bears the risk of defective issuance toward purchasers for value and without notice; a purchaser with notice gets nothing. 'Notice of the particular defect' is the statutory hinge, which is the role of the official warning.
quote: even though issued with a defect going to its validity, is valid in the hands of a purchaser for value and without notice of the particular defect

name: UCC § 8-303 (protected purchaser) and § 3-302 (holder in due course)
rule_or_holding: A purchaser takes free of adverse claims and defences only if he gives value and has no notice of them.
relevance_to_gonka: Bona fide purchaser doctrine in statutory form: value plus absence of notice. Notice defeats protection.
quote: "Protected purchaser" means a purchaser of a certificated or uncertificated security, or of an interest therein, who: (1) gives value; (2) does not have notice of any adverse claim to the security; and (3) obtains control of the certificated or uncertificated security.

name: UCC § 8-105 (notice of adverse claim) and § 1-202 (notice; knowledge)
rule_or_holding: For investment securities, notice means actual knowledge, wilful blindness or breach of a duty to investigate. Generally, notice is given by taking reasonable steps to inform, and is received when it comes to the person's attention or is duly delivered to a channel that person holds out for communications.
relevance_to_gonka: Cuts both ways. § 1-202(d) helps the project (giving notice means taking reasonable steps, whether or not the other actually learns of it). § 8-105 and § 1-202(e) help post-warning traders: a public post is not delivered to anyone in particular, and for securities the test is actual knowledge or wilful blindness.
quote: A person has notice of an adverse claim if: (1) the person knows of the adverse claim; (2) the person is aware of facts sufficient to indicate that there is a significant probability that the adverse claim exists and deliberately avoids information that would establish the existence of the adverse claim

name: In re Bernard L. Madoff Investment Securities LLC
forum: US Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
rule_or_holding: Customer claims are measured by cash deposited minus cash withdrawn (Net Investment Method), not by balances on fictitious statements.
relevance_to_gonka: When prices or balances were corrupted by the event, compensate real money lost, netted per person; do not compensate paper value, and do not let one victim's gain be paid for by another. For WGNK: per-address netting of buys and sells over the incident window.
quote: Use of the Last Statement Method in this case would have the absurd effect of treating fictitious and arbitrarily assigned paper profits as real and would give legal effect to Madoff's machinations.

name: Janvey v. Brown (Stanford receivership)
citation: No. 13-10266 (5th Cir. Sept. 11, 2014); reporter cite 767 F.3d 430 is from memory
forum: US Court of Appeals, Fifth Circuit
rule_or_holding: Investors who received back principal plus purported interest are net winners; the excess is recoverable as a fraudulent transfer because it was not received for reasonably equivalent value.
relevance_to_gonka: Confirms the netting logic from the other side: gains extracted from the corrupted system are not earnings. For a voluntary plan this supports netting, not clawback.
quote: they are 'net winners' in the Ponzi scheme

name: SIPA definition of net equity
rule_or_holding: A customer's net equity is the sum that would have been owed if all the customer's positions had been liquidated on the filing date, net of what the customer owes.
relevance_to_gonka: Statutory precedent for a single reference date for valuing every position and a net figure per customer.
quote: calculating the sum which would have been owed by the debtor to such customer if the debtor had liquidated, by sale or purchase on the filing date— (i) all securities positions of such customer

name: Chwee Kin Keong v Digilandmall.com Pte Ltd
rule_or_holding: A contract at an obviously mistaken price is void at common law if the buyer had actual knowledge of the mistake; constructive knowledge plus unconscionable conduct may justify equitable relief.
relevance_to_gonka: A trader who knows the asset is mispriced or compromised and snaps up the opportunity gets no protection of the bargain. Post-warning buyers resemble the snapping-up buyers. Also shows the actual/constructive knowledge distinction.
quote: Clearly suspecting a mistake, he pounced on the opportunity to make more money before the mistake was discovered. Thus, we do not think that the judge was wrong to have inferred actual knowledge. The apparent contracts are therefore void.

name: Quoine Pte Ltd v B2C2 Ltd
forum: Court of Appeal (appeal from the Singapore International Commercial Court)
rule_or_holding: Algorithmic trades executed at about 250 times the market rate stood; the exchange's unilateral reversal breached the contract. Unilateral mistake needs actual knowledge (common law) or constructive knowledge plus unconscionable conduct (equity), assessed in the programmer's mind when the code was written.
relevance_to_gonka: Mostly a counter-point: trades on a functioning venue are not undone merely because the price was abnormal, and bots do not read announcements, so 'notice' at the timestamp is a fiction for algorithmic or resting orders. Positive use: absent knowledge, pre-warning trades are legitimate and their losers are genuine victims.
quote: for unilateral mistake at common law, the non-mistaken party must have had actual knowledge of the mistaken party's mistake, and if this is established, the contract will be rendered void

name: Exchange clearly-erroneous-execution rules (NYSE Rule 7.10, Nasdaq Rule 11890 and harmonised sister rules)
citation: NYSE Chicago Rule 7.10, SEC Release 34-95825, Exhibit 5 (2022); NYSE Rule 7.10 and Nasdaq Rule 11890 numbering not checked
forum: Self-regulatory organisation rules approved by the SEC
rule_or_holding: Trades with an obvious error in a term may be reviewed on a request made within 30 minutes of execution and busted; any transaction occurring after the primary listing market declares a regulatory halt and before it ends is nullified.
relevance_to_gonka: The official declaration of a halt is a hard line: later trades are nullified, not compensated. The remedy (undoing trades within minutes by a neutral official) is unavailable on a DEX, which is why Gonka must compensate instead. The 30-minute windows show the reaction time-scale of organised markets.
quote: will nullify any transaction in a security that occurs after the primary listing market for such security declares a regulatory trading halt, suspension or pause with respect to such security and before such regulatory trading halt, suspension or pause with respect to such security has officially ended according to the primary listing market.

name: Knight Capital trading incident of 1 August 2012
citation: SEC Press Release 2013-222 (2013); administrative settlement under Exchange Act Rule 15c3-5
rule_or_holding: A faulty order router sent more than 4 million orders in 45 minutes; the firm lost more than $460 million and paid a $12 million penalty under the market access rule.
relevance_to_gonka: Context: the party whose systems failed bore the loss; counterparties without knowledge kept their bargains except where trades met clearly-erroneous thresholds (that last point is general knowledge, not verified here). Figures read through an automated fetch of the press release.
quote: suffered a loss of more than $460 million

name: Nasdaq news-pending trading halts (codes T1/T2)
citation: Nasdaq Trader, Trade Halt Codes; Nasdaq Rule 4120 (rule text not opened)
forum: Exchange operating practice; year is the date the page was read
rule_or_holding: Trading is halted pending the release of material news (T1) and while the news is being disseminated (T2), then resumed.
relevance_to_gonka: Organised markets do not rely on instant absorption: they stop trading while material news spreads. WGNK kept trading through the announcement, which makes a to-the-second cut-off harsher than its TradFi model and is the best justification for a short grace window. Typical halt length not verified.
quote: Trading is halted pending the release of material news.

name: Germany, HGB § 15(1)–(2) (publicity of the commercial register)
rule_or_holding: Before registration and publication a fact cannot be invoked against a third party unless he knew it. After publication the third party is bound, except for acts within fifteen days of publication if he proves he neither knew nor ought to have known the fact.
relevance_to_gonka: Closest analogy in direction (entity publishes officially, third parties are bound) and a ready three-zone template: before warning = protected unless actual knowledge; short window after = protected if the claimant shows lack of knowledge; later = bound. Best authority for a grace period with the burden of proof on the claimant.
quote: Ist die Tatsache eingetragen und bekanntgemacht worden, so muß ein Dritter sie gegen sich gelten lassen. Dies gilt nicht bei Rechtshandlungen, die innerhalb von fünfzehn Tagen nach der Bekanntmachung vorgenommen werden, sofern der Dritte beweist, daß er die Tatsache weder kannte noch kennen mußte.

name: EU Directive on company law, art. 16(6) (effect of disclosure against third parties)
citation: Directive (EU) 2017/1132, art. 16(6) (codifying the First Company Law Directive); original 2017 text read, later amendments not checked
rule_or_holding: Disclosed company particulars bind third parties only after official disclosure, and for transactions before the sixteenth day after disclosure they do not bind third parties who prove it was impossible for them to have known.
relevance_to_gonka: The HGB § 15(2) rule at EU level, so the 15-day grace after official publication is not a German peculiarity. Note the strict test inside the grace window.
quote: However, with regard to transactions taking place before the sixteenth day following the disclosure, the documents and particulars shall not be relied on as against third parties who prove that it was impossible for them to have had knowledge thereof.

name: Revised Uniform Partnership Act § 704(c) as enacted in Delaware (statement of dissociation; deemed notice)
citation: 6 Del. C. §§ 15-703(b), 15-704(c); uniform RUPA (1997) § 704(c) uses 90 days (not checked)
rule_or_holding: A non-partner is deemed to have notice of a partner's dissociation 60 days after the statement is filed; until then, and for up to a year, the former partner stays liable to those who reasonably relied and lacked notice.
relevance_to_gonka: A public filing becomes deemed notice only after a statutory lag. Authority that constructive notice starts later than publication.
quote: a person not a partner is deemed to have notice of the dissociation 60 days after the statement of dissociation is filed.

name: Product warnings and recall notices (Restatement (Second) of Torts § 402A cmt. j; comparative fault for ignored recalls)
citation: Restatement (Second) of Torts § 402A, comment j (1965); Restatement (Third) of Torts: Products Liability §§ 10, 11 (1998)
forum: American Law Institute; state case law
rule_or_holding: Comment j is cited for the idea that a seller who gives a warning may assume it will be read and heeded. An ignored recall notice can be argued as comparative fault, but commentary says the manufacturer is probably not fully exonerated.
relevance_to_gonka: Weak. No clear authority found that an ignored recall notice ends liability; at most it supports a reduction (comparative fault), which points to a gradient rather than a cut-off. Not recommended for the slide. Sources: search results only.

name: Basic Inc. v. Levinson
rule_or_holding: The fraud-on-the-market presumption of reliance is severed once the truth credibly enters the market: people who trade after the corrective statement have no connection with the wrong.
relevance_to_gonka: Closest market-law analogue of the 00:24:07 line: once the issuer's own explicit warning is out, later traders are no longer trading on a market distorted by the issuer's silence. Note the word 'credibly' - it is the reason a third-party alert at 18:28 is a weaker dividing line than the official warning.
quote: if, despite petitioners' allegedly fraudulent attempt to manipulate market price, news of the merger discussions credibly entered the market and dissipated the effects of the misstatements, those who traded Basic shares after the corrective statements would have no direct or indirect connection with the fraud.

name: Securities Act of 1933, s. 11(a) and (e)
rule_or_holding: Any acquirer of a security may sue for a misleading registration statement unless he knew of the untruth or omission when he acquired; damages are capped by the amount paid.
relevance_to_gonka: Statutory form of the two core ideas of the proposal: (i) knowledge at the moment of acquisition removes the claim; (ii) recovery is measured from the price actually paid, never more.
quote: any person acquiring such security (unless it is proved that at the time of such acquisition he knew of such untruth or omission) may, either at law or in equity, in any court of competent jurisdiction, sue

name: Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, Sch. 10 para. 6
rule_or_holding: No liability for misleading listing particulars/prospectus towards a person who acquired the securities with knowledge of the falsity or of the omitted matter.
