relevance_to_gonka: English statutory twin of A02: knowledge at acquisition is a complete answer. Supports treating buyers who bought after the explicit official warning as outside the mandatory tier.
quote: A person does not incur any liability under section 90(1) or (4) if he satisfies the court that the person suffering the loss acquired the securities in question with knowledge— (a) that the statement was false or misleading, (b) of the omitted matter, or (c) of the change or new matter, as the case may be.

name: Wertpapierhandelsgesetz (WpHG) § 97 - damages for failure to publish inside information without delay
rule_or_holding: An issuer that fails to publish inside information without undue delay must compensate a third party who buys after the omission and still holds when the information becomes known; no claim if the buyer knew the information when buying.
relevance_to_gonka: The single closest statutory model for the Gonka design: the protected class is exactly 'bought during the issuer's silence, still held when the truth came out', and knowledge at purchase excludes the claim. It applies to listed financial instruments, so for WGNK it is an analogy, not a directly applicable rule.
quote: (1) ... ist er einem Dritten zum Ersatz des durch die Unterlassung entstandenen Schadens verpflichtet, wenn der Dritte 1. die Finanzinstrumente nach der Unterlassung erwirbt und er bei Bekanntwerden der Insiderinformation noch Inhaber der Finanzinstrumente ist ... (3) Der Anspruch nach Absatz 1 besteht nicht, wenn der Dritte die Insiderinformation im Falle des Absatzes 1 Nr. 1 bei dem Erwerb ... kannte.

name: Smith v Baker & Sons
rule_or_holding: Volenti non fit injuria requires free acceptance of the risk; mere knowledge of the danger (scienti) is not consent.
relevance_to_gonka: Cuts against an all-or-nothing reading of the warning: a trader who merely could have known (or even knew) is not automatically treated as having accepted the whole loss. This is the doctrinal reason why post-warning treatment is a matter of apportionment (gradient) rather than an automatic total bar.
quote: I am unable to accede to the suggestion that the mere fact of his continuing at his work, with such knowledge and appreciation, will in every case necessarily imply his acceptance. (Lord Watson, as reproduced by the secondary source)

name: Law Reform (Contributory Negligence) Act 1945, s. 1(1)
rule_or_holding: The claimant's own fault no longer defeats the claim; damages are reduced to the extent the court thinks just and equitable having regard to the claimant's share in the responsibility.
relevance_to_gonka: Core common-law authority for the gradient option: fault of the trader after the warning reduces, but does not necessarily extinguish, compensation. Also shows that the fractions are a matter of 'just and equitable' judgment, not arithmetic.
quote: a claim in respect of that damage shall not be defeated by reason of the fault of the person suffering the damage, but the damages recoverable in respect thereof shall be reduced to such extent as the court thinks just and equitable having regard to the claimant’s share in the responsibility for the damage

name: Li v. Yellow Cab Co.
rule_or_holding: Replaced the all-or-nothing contributory negligence bar with comparative negligence (liability in proportion to fault); assumption of risk, so far as it is a variant of contributory negligence, is subsumed into apportionment.
relevance_to_gonka: Leading US statement that 'he knew the risk' is normally an apportionment factor, not a cliff. Directly supports a declining coefficient after 00:24:07 instead of an instant drop to zero.
quote: it must give way to a system of comparative negligence, which assesses liability in direct proportion to fault. ... last clear chance and assumption of risk (insofar as the latter doctrine is but a variant of contributory negligence) are to be subsumed under the general process of assessing liability in proportion to fault

name: Contributory Negligence and Personal Injuries Act 1953, s. 3(1)
rule_or_holding: Same apportionment rule as the English 1945 Act: claim not defeated by the claimant's fault; damages reduced as the court thinks just and equitable.
relevance_to_gonka: Shows the apportionment (not all-or-nothing) approach is shared by the main Asian crypto-litigation venue.
quote: a claim in respect of that damage shall not be defeated by reason of the fault of the person suffering the damage, but the damages recoverable in respect thereof shall be reduced to such extent as the court thinks just and equitable having regard to the claimant’s share in the responsibility for the damage.

name: Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch (BGB) § 254 - Mitverschulden
forum: Civil Code (official English translation of the Federal Ministry of Justice)
rule_or_holding: Where the injured person's fault contributed to the damage, liability and its extent depend on the circumstances, in particular on who mainly caused the damage; this includes failing to avert or mitigate the damage.
relevance_to_gonka: Civil-law anchor for the gradient: trading against an explicit warning is 'failing to avert the damage', which leads to a sliding reduction according to causal contribution - up to 100 % in clear cases - rather than a fixed rule.
quote: Where fault on the part of the injured person contributed to the occurrence of the damage, liability in damages as well as the extent of compensation to be provided depend on the circumstances, in particular on the extent to which the damage was caused mainly by one or the other party.

name: Civil Code of the Russian Federation, art. 404 (fault of the creditor)
forum: Civil Code (text read on an unofficial mirror, zakonrf.info)
rule_or_holding: If the breach resulted from the fault of both parties the court reduces the debtor's liability accordingly; it may also reduce it where the creditor intentionally or negligently contributed to the increase of losses or did not take reasonable measures to reduce them.
relevance_to_gonka: Russian-law equivalent of § 254 BGB: proportional reduction, including for failure to take reasonable steps to reduce one's own loss after being warned.
quote: Если неисполнение или ненадлежащее исполнение обязательства произошло по вине обеих сторон, суд соответственно уменьшает размер ответственности должника. Суд также вправе уменьшить размер ответственности должника, если кредитор умышленно или по неосторожности содействовал увеличению размера убытков ... либо не принял разумных мер к их уменьшению.

name: Civil Code of the Russian Federation, art. 1083 (fault of the victim)
forum: Civil Code (text read on an unofficial mirror, zakonrf.info)
rule_or_holding: Harm caused by the victim's own intent is not compensated; where the victim's gross negligence contributed to the harm or increased it, compensation must be reduced according to the degrees of fault.
relevance_to_gonka: Gives the two-level structure used in the proposal: deliberate risk-taking (buying a token one knows to be unbacked in order to speculate) = no compensation; gross carelessness = reduction, not exclusion. Ordinary (simple) carelessness of the victim does not reduce compensation in tort under this article.
quote: 1. Вред, возникший вследствие умысла потерпевшего, возмещению не подлежит. 2. Если грубая неосторожность самого потерпевшего содействовала возникновению или увеличению вреда, в зависимости от степени вины потерпевшего и причинителя вреда размер возмещения должен быть уменьшен.

name: Cour de cassation - no duty of the victim to mitigate
citation: Cass. 2e civ., 19 June 2003, nos. 01-13.289 and 00-22.302; reaffirmed Cass. 1re civ., 2 July 2014 (pourvoi number not verified)
rule_or_holding: The author of a harm must repair all its consequences; the victim is not obliged to limit the loss in the interest of the person liable (no general duty to mitigate in French law, including for economic loss).
relevance_to_gonka: Important counter-authority to a hard cut-off: under the French approach, failure to react to a warning does not by itself reduce compensation (only a causal fault of the victim does). Supports the 'full compensation after the warning' option, or at least a generous gradient.
quote: « l’auteur d’un dommage doit en réparer toutes les conséquences et la victime n’est pas tenue de limiter son préjudice dans l’intérêt du responsable » (as quoted by the secondary source for the 2 July 2014 decision)

name: French general principle: fault of the victim gives partial exoneration
citation: Case law under art. 1240-1241 Code civil (formerly 1382-1383); Cass. 2e civ., 4 Nov. 2010, no. 09-65.947 (acceptance of risk not opposable against liability for things)
rule_or_holding: A fault of the victim that contributed to the harm leads to partial exoneration (shared liability), total only if it amounts to force majeure; 'acceptation des risques' has been largely abandoned as a bar.
relevance_to_gonka: France reaches a gradient through 'partage de responsabilité' while rejecting acceptance-of-risk as an automatic bar. NOT opened in a primary source: Légifrance and the court-of-appeal fiche were unreachable (anti-bot page / maintenance). Search results also report an Assemblée plénière decision of 29 May 2026 narrowing partial exoneration for bodily injury - not verified.

name: Merck & Co. v. Reynolds
rule_or_holding: 'Discovery' covers facts actually known and facts a reasonably diligent plaintiff would have known; but mere 'storm warnings' / inquiry notice do not themselves start the clock - the question is when a diligent person would actually have discovered the facts.
relevance_to_gonka: Two-edged. For an earlier cut-off: a diligent trader is charged with what he would have found (public security alert at 18:28, a dozen press articles by 22:30, a -95 % chart). Against it: unconfirmed warnings only trigger a duty to look further; knowledge is fixed at the point when diligent inquiry would have produced the facts - i.e. the official confirmation.
quote: We consequently hold that “discovery” as used in this statute encompasses not only those facts the plaintiff actually knew, but also those facts a reasonably diligent plaintiff would have known.

name: Law of Property Act 1925, s. 199(1)(ii)(a)
rule_or_holding: Statutory definition of constructive notice: a purchaser is fixed with what is within his own knowledge or would have come to his knowledge had he made the inquiries he ought reasonably to have made.
relevance_to_gonka: The classical test that the 'earlier cut-off' camp would invoke: what inquiries ought a buyer of a token that had just fallen 95 % reasonably to have made? (The provision concerns land; it is cited for the definition.)
quote: it is within his own knowledge, or would have come to his knowledge if such inquiries and inspections had been made as ought reasonably to have been made by him

name: Manchester Trust v Furness
rule_or_holding: Lindley LJ: the equitable doctrine of constructive notice should not be extended to commercial transactions, where there is no time to investigate.
relevance_to_gonka: Standard answer to the 'professionals had constructive notice at 18:28' argument: in fast commercial dealing English courts are reluctant to charge parties with what they could have found out. Source could not be opened (BAILII returned 403, secondary site had an expired certificate); wording taken from memory and search snippets - do not quote without checking the law report.

name: Federal Crop Insurance Corp. v. Merrill
rule_or_holding: Publication through the legally designated official channel gives legal notice of the contents to everyone, regardless of actual knowledge or hardship from innocent ignorance.
relevance_to_gonka: Strongest authority for a bright line at the moment of official publication: once the issuer has spoken through its designated official channel, 'I did not see it' is not an answer. The limit of the analogy: the Federal Register is designated by statute, a project's X account is designated only by its own practice.
quote: Just as everyone is charged with knowledge of the United States Statutes at Large, Congress has provided that the appearance of rules and regulations in the Federal Register gives legal notice of their contents.

name: Marine Insurance Act 1906, s. 62(3)
rule_or_holding: The duty to act runs from receipt of reliable information; where the information is of a doubtful character the person is entitled to a reasonable time to make inquiry.
relevance_to_gonka: Statutory recognition of exactly the distinction in the Gonka timeline: an unconfirmed third-party alert (18:28) is 'information of a doubtful character' giving time to inquire; the official confirmation/warning (00:18-00:24) is 'reliable information'. Supports both the official warning as the line and a short grace period after it.
quote: Notice of abandonment must be given with reasonable diligence after the receipt of reliable information of the loss, but where the information is of a doubtful character the assured is entitled to a reasonable time to make inquiry.

name: Mullane v. Central Hanover Bank & Trust Co.
rule_or_holding: Notice must be reasonably calculated, under all the circumstances, to apprise interested parties, must reasonably convey the information and must leave a reasonable time to respond; a 'mere gesture' is not notice. Publication is acceptable for persons who cannot be individually identified.
relevance_to_gonka: Benchmark for judging the 00:24:07 post: (i) for anonymous on-chain holders publication is the only feasible means, so publication on the official channel is adequate in kind; (ii) but the means must be those 'one desirous of actually informing' would use - X only, with the website banner 11.6 hours later, is the weak point; (iii) 'reasonable time' supports a grace period after the warning.
quote: An elementary and fundamental requirement of due process in any proceeding which is to be accorded finality is notice reasonably calculated, under all the circumstances, to apprise interested parties ... it must afford a reasonable time for those interested to make their appearance ... The means employed must be such as one desirous of actually informing the absentee might reasonably adopt to accomplish it.

name: SEC Report of Investigation: Netflix, Inc., and Reed Hastings
citation: Exchange Act Release No. 69279 (2 Apr. 2013); SEC press release 2013-51
forum: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (s. 21(a) report)
rule_or_holding: Social media can be a valid channel for material disclosure, but only if the market has been alerted in advance to which channels the issuer uses; a channel not previously flagged is unlikely to qualify.
relevance_to_gonka: Directly on point for 'is a post on X legally effective notice?'. Answer: yes if the project's X account is its established, publicly designated announcement channel (it should be documented that it was); otherwise the later website banner (~12:03) becomes the safer notice date. For the future: publish a standing list of official incident channels.
quote: We emphasize for issuers that the steps taken to alert the market about which forms of communication a company intends to use for the dissemination of material, non-public information, including the social media channels that may be used ... are critical to the fair and efficient disclosure of information. Without such notice, the investing public would be forced to keep pace with a changing and expanding universe of potential disclosure channels, a virtually impossible task.

name: Regulation FD - definition of public disclosure
rule_or_holding: Public disclosure may be made by any method (or combination) reasonably designed to provide broad, non-exclusionary distribution of the information to the public.
relevance_to_gonka: Test to apply to the 00:24:07 post: was X alone 'reasonably designed' for broad distribution to WGNK traders? Arguably yes for a crypto-native audience (X is the industry's de facto wire), with the caveat in B02.
quote: another method (or combination of methods) of disclosure that is reasonably designed to provide broad, non-exclusionary distribution of the information to the public

name: SEC v. Texas Gulf Sulphur Co.
citation: 401 F.2d 833 (2d Cir. 1968) (en banc), passage at fn. 18
forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
rule_or_holding: Information is not 'public' at the instant of release: it must have had time to appear over the media of widest circulation, and for news not readily translatable into action a 'reasonable waiting period' for absorption may be required.
relevance_to_gonka: Best case-law support for a short grace step after 00:24:07 instead of an instant cliff. In the Gonka timeline the 'media of widest circulation' moment is the press repetition of the warning at 01:35 UTC (71 minutes after the post) - an objective anchor for the end of the first step.
quote: at the minimum Coates should have waited until the news could reasonably have been expected to appear over the media of widest circulation, the Dow Jones broad tape ... where the news is of a sort which is not readily translatable into investment action, insiders may not take advantage of their advance opportunity to evaluate the information by acting immediately upon dissemination.

name: Ganino v. Citizens Utilities Co.
forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
rule_or_holding: 'Truth-on-the-market': information counts as known to the market only if conveyed with a degree of intensity and credibility sufficient to counter-balance the misleading impression; the defence is intensely fact-specific.
relevance_to_gonka: Main answer to the 'everyone knew at 18:28' objection: a security firm's tweet and early press reports, while the issuer itself stayed silent for six hours, arguably lacked the intensity and credibility of an official statement. Equally, it warns that the answer is fact-specific - by 22:30 a dozen outlets had reported the hack.
quote: the corrective information must be conveyed to the public “with a degree of intensity and credibility sufficient to counter-balance effectively any misleading information created by” the alleged misstatements. ... The truth-on-the-market defense is intensely fact-specific

name: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 (MiCA), art. 88(1)
rule_or_holding: Issuers, offerors and persons seeking admission to trading of crypto-assets must inform the public of inside information as soon as possible, in a manner enabling fast access and timely assessment, and must post it on their website.
relevance_to_gonka: (i) Legislative standard for crypto-asset incident disclosure: 'as soon as possible' and 'on their website'. Measured against it, the 6h22m between exploit and warning is the period of the issuer's own default (basis for treating pre-warning losses as an obligation), and the website banner at ~12:03 is the first moment the website requirement was met (argument for a later effective-notice date). (ii) Applies only if the token is within MiCA's scope (admitted to trading on a trading platform for crypto-assets); for WGNK this must be checked - otherwise it is an analogy.
quote: Issuers, offerors and persons seeking admission to trading shall inform the public as soon as possible of inside information referred to in Article 87 that directly concerns them, in a manner that enables fast access as well as complete, correct and timely assessment of the information by the public. ... shall post and maintain on their website, for a period of at least five years, all inside information that they are required to disclose publicly.

name: Regulation (EU) No 596/2014 (Market Abuse Regulation), art. 17(1)
rule_or_holding: Issuers of financial instruments must inform the public as soon as possible of inside information directly concerning them, in a manner enabling fast access and complete, correct and timely assessment.
relevance_to_gonka: The securities-market original of MiCA art. 88; shows the 'as soon as possible / fast access' standard is the settled European benchmark for when an issuer must speak.
quote: An issuer shall inform the public as soon as possible of inside information which directly concerns that issuer.

name: Parker v South Eastern Railway Co
rule_or_holding: A person is bound by conditions he did not read only if he was given reasonable notice of them (Mellish LJ's three questions).
relevance_to_gonka: Origin of the 'reasonably sufficient notice' test in English law: the question is not whether the trader actually read the warning but whether what the project did was reasonably sufficient to bring it to traders' attention.
quote: if he knew there was writing, and knew or believed that the writing contained conditions, then he is bound by the conditions (Mellish LJ, as reproduced by the secondary source)

name: Thornton v Shoe Lane Parking Ltd; Interfoto Picture Library Ltd v Stiletto Visual Programmes Ltd
rule_or_holding: The more onerous or unusual the consequence, the more explicit the notice must be (Lord Denning's 'red hand' dictum; Interfoto: a 'particularly onerous or unusual' term needs special notice).
relevance_to_gonka: Losing all compensation is a heavy consequence, so the notice that triggers it should be prominent and explicit. The 00:24:07 text ('Do not trade WGNK, do not use the bridge, withdraw liquidity') is explicit in content; its prominence (X only until the ~12:03 website banner) is the vulnerable point.
quote: In order to give sufficient notice, it would need to be printed in red ink with a red hand pointing to it – or something equally startling. (Lord Denning MR, as reproduced by the secondary source)

name: Nasdaq trade halt codes T1 / T2 / T3
forum: Exchange market practice (official Nasdaq reference page)
rule_or_holding: Trading is halted pending material news (T1), stays halted while the news is being disseminated (T2) and resumes only after the news has been fully disseminated (T3).
relevance_to_gonka: Organised markets do not let anyone trade in the minutes between a material announcement and its full dissemination. A DEX pool cannot be halted, so a grace step after the warning is the functional substitute for the halt-until-disseminated practice.
quote: T1 Halt - News Pending Trading is halted pending the release of material news. T2 Halt - News Released The news has begun the dissemination process through a Regulation FD compliant method(s). ... T3 News and Resumption Times The news has been fully disseminated through a Regulation FD compliant method(s)

name: Uniform Commercial Code § 4-406(c), (d)
rule_or_holding: After the bank makes a statement available, the customer must examine it with reasonable promptness; the customer is precluded only after a reasonable period, not exceeding 30 days.
relevance_to_gonka: Example of a 'reasonable time to react after notice' rule: responsibility shifts to the notified person only after a reasonable period, not at the instant the notice is made available.
quote: the customer must exercise reasonable promptness in examining the statement or the items ... after the customer had been afforded a reasonable period of time, not exceeding 30 days, in which to examine the item or statement of account and notify the bank.

name: Cammer v. Bloom
forum: U.S. District Court, District of New Jersey
rule_or_holding: Five factors of an efficient market: weekly trading volume, analyst coverage, market makers/arbitrageurs, Form S-3 eligibility and - the essence - a cause-and-effect relationship between unexpected news and an immediate price response.
relevance_to_gonka: Courts presume instant absorption only for markets that pass these tests. A thin DEX pool of a bridged token (no analysts, no designated market makers, liquidity being withdrawn) would score poorly, so one cannot assume that the warning was 'in the price' and known to all at 00:24:07 - an argument for a grace step.
quote: it would be helpful to a plaintiff seeking to allege an efficient market to allege empirical facts showing a cause and effect relationship between unexpected corporate events or financial releases and an immediate response in the stock price. This, after all, is the essence of an efficient market and the foundation for the fraud on the market theory.

name: In re Petrobras Securities
forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
rule_or_holding: Affirmed a finding of market efficiency made on a combination of direct and indirect evidence; notes that the Cammer factors are routinely applied by district courts but that the Circuit has not adopted a fixed test.
relevance_to_gonka: Confirms that 'how fast did the market know' is a question of evidence for the particular market, not a legal presumption - the project should support the chosen steps with WGNK's own price/volume reaction data.
quote: We find no abuse of discretion in the district court’s determination that Plaintiffs met their burden under Basic with a combination of direct and indirect evidence of market efficiency.

name: Halliburton Co. v. Erica P. John Fund, Inc. (Halliburton II)
rule_or_holding: Market efficiency is a matter of degree, not a binary; the Court refuses to adopt any particular theory of how quickly and completely public information is reflected in price.
relevance_to_gonka: Highest-level authority that absorption of news is gradual and a matter of proof - the conceptual basis for a gradient instead of an instant switch.
quote: in making the presumption rebuttable, Basic recognized that market efficiency is a matter of degree and accordingly made it a matter of proof.

name: Patell & Wolfson, 'The intraday speed of adjustment of stock prices to earnings and dividend announcements'
forum: Peer-reviewed study (abstract on the Stanford GSB page)
rule_or_holding: Prices of listed stocks begin to react within a few minutes of a newswire release and trading-rule profits disappear in five to ten minutes, but disturbances in variance persist for several hours into the next trading day.
relevance_to_gonka: Shows both things at once: the bulk of absorption in a liquid market takes minutes (so a one-hour first step is generous, not stingy), while full settling takes hours to a day (so a tail out to 24 h is not arbitrary).
quote: The initial price reaction is evident in the first pair of price changes following the release (i.e., within a few minutes, at most). The returns earned by simple trading rules dissipate within five to ten minutes ... Disturbances in the variance and serial correlation persist for several hours and extend into the following trading day.

name: Busse & Green, 'Market efficiency in real time'
rule_or_holding: After on-air CNBC reports prices respond within seconds; positive reports are fully incorporated within about one minute, negative ones more gradually.
relevance_to_gonka: Further evidence that in liquid markets absorption is a matter of minutes. Publisher page returned 403; details known only from search-result abstracts - not opened.

name: Azar, Olivas & Sinha, 'The Price of Processing: Information Frictions and Market Efficiency in DeFi'
citation: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Reports no. 1153 (April 2025)
forum: Staff report, 49 DeFi hacks, Sept. 2020 - March 2024, minute-level prices
rule_or_holding: After a DeFi hack the governance token falls about 27 % over 24 hours; about 36 % of that decline happens before the first public announcement (sophisticated traders read the chain); the price stabilises 9-24 hours after the hack. Median lag from hack to first public disclosure: 1 h 51 min (quartiles 43 min and 5 h 45 min).
relevance_to_gonka: The only rigorous crypto-specific study found. (i) Supports the gradient: even for hacks, information becomes 'common knowledge' over hours, and prices settle within 9-24 h - an empirical anchor for ending the tail at 24 h. (ii) Supports the 'earlier cut-off for professionals' objection: sophisticated actors trade on the hack well before any announcement. (iii) Benchmark for Gonka: first public alert after 26 minutes (faster than the 25th percentile), official warning after 6 h 22 min (slower than the 75th percentile of first disclosures).
quote: approximately 36 percent of the total 24-hour price decline (∼27 percent) materializes before the public announcement ... The decline continues over the subsequent hours, stabilizing around -26 percent between 9 and 24 hours after the initial transaction.

name: Decurity, 'Off the Cliff: How Token Prices Are Affected by Hacks'
rule_or_holding: Reaction speed after hacks is very uneven: some tokens fall within 5 minutes, more than half show no 1 % move in the first hour; many keep declining for days.
relevance_to_gonka: Shows that crypto markets after hacks are far from the 'minutes' of listed equities - supports a tail of hours rather than a cliff, and warns that 24 h may be short for some tokens. Read through an automated page summary; several numeric fields were missing.
quote: KiloEx, Vestra, Shezmu, Rodeo Finance, Multichain - all these tokens dropped 1% within 5 minutes of the hack.

name: Regulation E (Electronic Fund Transfers) - consumer liability tiers
forum: Federal regulation (CFPB; originally Federal Reserve Board)
rule_or_holding: Loss allocation steps up with the time elapsed after the consumer learns of the problem: up to $50 if reported within 2 business days; up to $500 after that; unlimited for transfers after 60 days from the statement; time limits extended for extenuating circumstances.
relevance_to_gonka: The cleanest regulatory precedent for the gradient: bright-line time tiers after notice, each shifting more of the loss to the person who had been notified, with a hardship extension. It validates the form (steps by elapsed time) though not the specific fractions. Note the scale: days, not hours.
quote: If the consumer notifies the financial institution within two business days after learning of the loss or theft of the access device, the consumer's liability shall not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers that occur before notice to the financial institution.

name: Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2), art. 74
rule_or_holding: Three-level allocation: payer bears at most EUR 50 of unauthorised payments; bears everything if he acted fraudulently or with intent/gross negligence; bears nothing after he has notified the provider.
relevance_to_gonka: European example of loss allocation that depends on (a) the degree of the victim's fault and (b) the moment of notification - the same two variables as the Gonka gradient.
quote: the payer may be obliged to bear the losses relating to any unauthorised payment transactions, up to a maximum of EUR 50 ... The payer shall not bear any financial consequences resulting from use of the lost, stolen or misappropriated payment instrument after notification

name: Private Securities Litigation Reform Act - 90-day look-back
rule_or_holding: Damages are capped by reference to the mean trading price over the 90 days after the corrective information is disseminated (or until the plaintiff sells, if earlier).
relevance_to_gonka: Congress itself assumed that a market needs time after a corrective disclosure before the price is a fair measure of loss, and that later recovery of the price reduces the loss. Supports (i) a post-warning window rather than an instant measurement and (ii) netting later price recovery against the loss.
quote: the award of damages to the plaintiff shall not exceed the difference between the purchase or sale price paid or received, as appropriate, by the plaintiff for the subject security and the mean trading price of that security during the 90-day period beginning on the date on which the information correcting the misstatement or omission that is the basis for the action is disseminated to the market.

name: Directive 2011/83/EU (Consumer Rights), art. 9(1)
rule_or_holding: Consumers have 14 days to withdraw from distance contracts without giving reasons.
relevance_to_gonka: Illustrates that consumer law routinely gives fixed grace periods to undo a decision. Weak analogy for trading (financial services with price fluctuation are typically excluded from withdrawal rights), cited only to show that fixed grace periods are an accepted technique.
quote: the consumer shall have a period of 14 days to withdraw from a distance or off-premises contract, without giving any reason

name: KyberSwap Elastic exploit - Treasury Grant Program
rule_or_holding: Victims chose between 60 % of the reference value in stablecoins vested over 3 months, or 100 % vested over 12 months (or opting out).
relevance_to_gonka: Precedent for a sliding scale in a DeFi compensation programme (here: amount traded against time), and for offering affected users a menu of options rather than a single rule.
quote: The first option provides the USD stablecoins equivalent to 60% of the reference value of affected assets, vested over 3 months. The second offers the USD stablecoins equivalent to 100% of the reference value, vested over 12 months.

name: Terra 2.0 airdrop (Terra governance proposal 1623)
rule_or_holding: New tokens were allocated in separate buckets for pre-attack and post-attack holders: 35 % pre-attack LUNA, 10 % pre-attack (a)UST, 10 % post-attack LUNA, 15 % post-attack UST, 30 % community pool.
relevance_to_gonka: Largest precedent for treating people who held before the event and people who bought after it as distinct classes with different, non-zero entitlements - i.e. the middle option of the Gonka design. (The post-attack UST share was reportedly cut from 20 % to 15 % after criticism that it rewarded speculators - not verified.)
quote: 35% to pre-attack LUNA holders. 10% to pre-attack UST holders. 10% to post-attack LUNA holders. 15% to post-attack UST holders.

name: Cover Protocol infinite-mint exploit - compensation snapshot
rule_or_holding: After an unbacked infinite mint crashed the token, the team compensated by a snapshot taken at the last block before the exploit; everyone who bought after the exploit began was outside the plan. The team also told users not to buy the token.
relevance_to_gonka: The closest factual twin (unbacked mint, price collapse, 'do not buy' warning). It is the precedent for the strictest possible line (cut-off at the exploit itself) - and for the backlash it causes: holders demanded a snapshot at the moment of the public announcement because 'many people did not know'. The Gonka proposal's line at the official warning is exactly what those critics asked for.
quote: the Cover Protocol team took a snapshot at block height 11,541,218, the last transaction block before the exploit began. (Cointelegraph) / “You should make a snapshot from the moment you announced via Twitter that the contract got exploited.” (user quoted by Bitcoin.com News)

name: Binance SAFU compensation for the COVER incident
rule_or_holding: Binance paid about USD 10.1 million from its SAFU fund to its users who held or traded COVER between the protocol's snapshot time and the moment Binance stopped trading - the very group the protocol's plan left out.
relevance_to_gonka: Precedent for the Gonka 'obligation' tier: a responsible venue compensated those who traded between the exploit and the moment trading was officially stopped, i.e. the cut-off was the official stop, not the exploit. Users who merely deposited tokens in that window (potential opportunists) were excluded.
quote: a lot of Binance users who bought COVER on the trading platform after COVER's proposed snapshot time (December 28, at 8:11:06 AM UTC) would have their tokens become worthless ... Binance will not make any additional compensation for users that only deposited tokens between the ETH Snapshot Time and the Trading Stop Time. (FXStreet report of the Binance statement)

name: pGALA / pNetwork bridge incident
rule_or_holding: After an unbacked mint of the bridged token, pNetwork warned that newly bought pGALA was not redeemable 1:1, re-issued the token to pre-incident holders by snapshot, and reportedly assured post-incident buyers that they would get back the BNB they had spent.
relevance_to_gonka: Bridge-token precedent for the 'price paid, not cheap tokens' rule: post-incident buyers were to be made whole in what they spent, not given 1:1 new tokens for tokens bought at a crashed price. The operator's primary post-mortem (Medium) could not be opened (403); the refund statement rests on one press report.
quote: the team also assured that those who bought their pGALA after the pool began draining would receive their spent BNB back. (FXStreet)

name: bOSMO minting bug - compensation plan
rule_or_holding: A compensation plan for an under-backed token excludes people who bought after the eligibility snapshot.
relevance_to_gonka: Recent example that a hard snapshot excluding later buyers remains the default industry technique. Terms of the plan were not available in the source.
quote: A compensation plan excludes people who bought bOSMO after a snapshot used to determine eligibility.

name: Meter - post-attack snapshot and migration
rule_or_holding: Reported design: tokens held at the snapshot are swapped 1:1, tokens bought after the snapshot and still held are swapped at 10:1, with limited compensation for post-snapshot buyers on centralised exchanges.
relevance_to_gonka: If accurate, a direct precedent for a non-zero but heavily discounted entitlement for post-snapshot buyers (10 %), close to the Gonka 1/8 tier. The post could not be opened (Medium 403) and a follow-up search did not confirm the 10:1 figure - known only from a search-result summary. Do not cite without checking.

name: Bitfinex 2016 hack - socialised 36 % haircut and BFX tokens
rule_or_holding: Bitfinex reduced all customer balances by about 36 %, credited BFX tokens for the loss and later redeemed them at face value.
relevance_to_gonka: Shows the other extreme of loss allocation (everyone shares pro rata regardless of timing or fault). Known from search results only; not opened.

name: Dura Pharmaceuticals, Inc. v. Broudo
rule_or_holding: Securities-fraud law exists to compensate losses actually caused by the wrong, not to insure investors against market losses.
relevance_to_gonka: Works in two directions: (i) against compensating anyone whose loss stems from ordinary market risk taken with open eyes (post-warning dip buyers); (ii) for the net-loss rule - compensate only the loss caused by the hack, after netting gains.
quote: not to provide investors with broad insurance against market losses, but to protect them against those economic losses that misrepresentations actually cause.

name: Chiarella v. United States; Basic Inc. v. Levinson, n. 17
rule_or_holding: Silence is actionable only where there is a duty to speak; absent such a duty, silence is not misleading.
relevance_to_gonka: Candid limit on the 'misrepresentation by silence' basis: the six hours of official silence create liability only if some rule obliged the project to speak (a disclosure regime such as MiCA art. 88, its own terms or prior statements, or a special relationship). Without that, silence alone is not a legal wrong in US law.
quote: When an allegation of fraud is based upon nondisclosure, there can be no fraud absent a duty to speak. (Chiarella) / Silence, absent a duty to disclose, is not misleading under Rule 10b-5. (Basic, n. 17)

name: Risley v. Universal Navigation Inc. (Uniswap)
citation: No. 22 Civ. 2780 (KPF), 690 F. Supp. 3d 195 (S.D.N.Y. 29 Aug. 2023); aff'd in part, vacated in part by summary order (2d Cir. 26 Feb. 2025); remaining state claims reportedly dismissed 2 Mar. 2026
forum: U.S. District Court, S.D.N.Y. (appeal: Second Circuit)
rule_or_holding: Developers of a decentralised exchange protocol are not liable under the federal securities laws for losses caused by third parties who misused the platform.
relevance_to_gonka: Leading authority for the 'no legal duty to secondary-market traders' position: a court will not readily make the authors of protocol code pay for a third party's wrongdoing on a DEX. District opinion read in a law-firm-hosted copy of the court's order; the appellate summary order and the 2026 dismissal are known from search results only.
quote: it defies logic that a drafter of computer code underlying a particular software platform could be liable under Section 29(b) for a third-party’s misuse of that platform.

name: Sarcuni v. bZx DAO
forum: U.S. District Court, S.D. California (motion to dismiss)
rule_or_holding: Users who lost funds in a protocol hack plausibly alleged that the protocol's operators owed them a duty of reasonable care in managing the protocol (six-factor 'special relationship' test), although negligence liability for pure economic loss is 'the exception, not the rule'; a hack by itself does not prove breach.
relevance_to_gonka: Best authority that a negligence-based obligation of a bridge operator can exist - but note its limits: pleading stage only; the plaintiffs were the protocol's own users whose deposited funds were stolen, not secondary-market buyers of a devalued token; breach must still be shown.
quote: the Court finds that Plaintiffs have alleged that the bZx DAO had a duty to exercise reasonable care with respect to their management of the protocol. ... “liability in negligence for purely economic losses . . . is ‘the exception, not the rule.’”

name: Tulip Trading Ltd v Van der Laan (Bitcoin Association for BSV)
rule_or_holding: It is seriously arguable (no more) that developers who control a crypto network owe fiduciary or tortious duties to owners of the assets; the question was sent to trial and never decided on the merits (the claim was later discontinued - from recollection, not verified).
relevance_to_gonka: English position on a duty of developers/operators: open, arguable, undecided. It supports describing the project's responsibility as a credible litigation risk, not an established duty.
quote: The conclusion is not that there is a fiduciary duty in law in the circumstances alleged by Tulip, only that the case advanced raises a serious issue to be tried.

name: Spandeck Engineering (S) Pte Ltd v Defence Science & Technology Agency
rule_or_holding: A single two-stage test (proximity, then policy), preceded by factual foreseeability, governs the duty of care for all kinds of damage including pure economic loss; on the facts no duty was found.
relevance_to_gonka: In Singapore a holder would have to show proximity between himself and the bridge operator. Plausible for direct bridge users and liquidity providers; hard for an anonymous buyer on a DEX after the hack (indeterminate class, loss flowing from his own purchase decision).
quote: This test is a two-stage test, comprising of, first, proximity and, second, policy considerations.

name: Caparo Industries plc v Dickman
rule_or_holding: No duty of care for pure economic loss to an indeterminate class (investors relying on audited accounts) without foreseeability, proximity and it being fair, just and reasonable.
relevance_to_gonka: The standard English obstacle to a negligence claim by market purchasers against the bridge operator. Not opened (BAILII returned 403); stated from general knowledge.

name: Uniform Commercial Code § 8-210 (Overissue)
rule_or_holding: Securities issued in excess of what the issuer has power to issue are not validated; the person entitled may compel the issuer to buy and deliver a genuine security if one is reasonably available, otherwise may recover the price that he or the last purchaser for value paid, with interest.
relevance_to_gonka: The nearest black-letter rule for 'unbacked tokens that should never have existed': the holder does not get to keep the over-issued instrument as if valid; he gets either a genuine one or the price paid. This is the rule 'buyers get back the price paid, not cheap tokens'. Limits: it binds the issuer for its own over-issue of securities; here the mint was by an attacker and WGNK may not be a 'security' - analogy only.
quote: If a security is not reasonably available for purchase, a person entitled to issue or validation may recover from the issuer the price the person or the last purchaser for value paid for it with interest from the date of the person's demand.

name: In re Bernard L. Madoff Investment Securities LLC (net equity decision)
forum: U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
rule_or_holding: Customer claims in a fraud are measured by the net investment method (cash in minus cash out); fictitious paper profits are not recognised, and those who already took out more than they put in do not share.
relevance_to_gonka: Best judicial authority for 'nobody profits from the hack': compute each person's net position across all his trades, pay net losers only, and ignore paper values created by the wrong.
quote: Use of the Last Statement Method in this case would have the absurd effect of treating fictitious and arbitrarily assigned paper profits as real and would give legal effect to Madoff’s machinations.

name: SIPC - 'What SIPC Protects'
citation: Securities Investor Protection Corporation, official guidance
rule_or_holding: Even statutory investor protection restores custody of assets only; it does not cover a decline in the value of securities.
relevance_to_gonka: Benchmark for the moral-hazard objection: no mainstream protection scheme insures the price at which someone chose to buy. Supports limiting the mandatory tier to losses caused by the hack and by the period of official silence.
quote: SIPC does not protect against the decline in value of your securities.

name: Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co
rule_or_holding: A public promise to pay anyone who meets stated conditions is a binding unilateral offer once the conditions are met (civil-law parallels: § 657 BGB 'Auslobung'; arts. 1055-1056 Russian Civil Code, public promise of reward).
relevance_to_gonka: The most honest legal source of the word 'obligation' in the proposal: once the project publicly commits to compensate pre-warning net losses on stated terms, the commitment itself becomes enforceable - whatever the strength of the underlying tort claims. It also means the published terms must be drafted with care. Not opened; stated from general knowledge.

name: Quoine Pte Ltd v B2C2 Ltd
forum: Court of Appeal (appeal from the Singapore International Commercial Court)
rule_or_holding: Completed crypto trades executed at abnormal prices by algorithms were not unwound; the platform's unilateral reversal was a breach; mistake doctrines apply narrowly.
relevance_to_gonka: Courts are reluctant to undo completed crypto trades, even at absurd prices. Hence trades during the hack window stand, and relief can realistically come only from a compensation programme. Judgment page could not be opened (eLitigation returned 'not found'); stated from general knowledge.

name: Statute of the International Court of Justice, art. 34(1)
rule_or_holding: Only states may be parties before the ICJ; private persons and companies have no standing.
relevance_to_gonka: Authoritative, quotable basis for the statement that there is no international court for disputes between a crypto project and token holders. Such disputes go to national courts (or to arbitration, only if agreed).
quote: Only states may be parties in cases before the Court.

name: Regulation (EC) No 864/2007 (Rome II), art. 4(1)
rule_or_holding: The law applicable to a tort is the law of the country in which the damage occurs, irrespective of where the event giving rise to it occurred.
relevance_to_gonka: In EU courts each holder's claim would in principle be governed by the law of the place where his loss occurred - so a single hack can be judged under dozens of national laws. This is why the proposal is built on principles common to all major systems rather than on one statute.
quote: the law applicable to a non-contractual obligation arising out of a tort/delict shall be the law of the country in which the damage occurs irrespective of the country in which the event giving rise to the damage occurred

name: Law Commission of England and Wales - 'Digital assets and electronic trade documents in private international law'
citation: Project page; call for evidence 22 Feb. 2024; consultation paper 5 June 2025 (closed 8 Sept. 2025); final report expected 2026
rule_or_holding: Existing rules on 'which court, which law' rest on a territorial premise that crypto-tokens and distributed ledgers challenge; for wholly decentralised uses the Commission provisionally proposes that courts weigh a range of factors (including the parties' legitimate expectations) instead of locating a single applicable law.
relevance_to_gonka: Authoritative confirmation that (i) these disputes are decided by national courts under national conflict rules, and (ii) those rules are themselves unsettled for decentralised systems. No final report was found as of November 2026.
quote: modern technologies challenge the territorial premise on which the existing rules of private international law have been developed.

name: UNIDROIT Principles on Digital Assets and Private Law
rule_or_holding: Non-binding recommendations to national legislators; Principle 5 offers a 'waterfall' for the law governing proprietary issues (law specified in the asset, then in the system, then fallback options).
relevance_to_gonka: Confirms that the international layer consists of soft law addressed to national legislators, with no international adjudicator. Known from search-result summaries only; text not opened.
